dialogue.speaker: Old Keeper
dialogue.text: Halt, traveler. You have the look of someone seeking the deep dark.

default.speaker: Old Keeper
default.text: Halt, traveler. You have the look of someone seeking the deep dark.

default.speaker: Old Keeper
default.text: I was a Lightkeeper once... before the relays failed and the shadows crept in.

default.speaker: Old Keeper
default.text: The creatures down there feed on broken light. They'll take everything from you if you let them.

default.speaker: Old Keeper
default.text: A word of advice: never carry more than you can afford to lose. Death has a price in these crypts.

default.speaker: Old Keeper
default.text: Now go. The stairs await, and the dark won't keep itself at bay.

has_key.speaker: Old Keeper
has_key.text: You found the iron key? Good. The locked door to the east should yield to it.

has_key.speaker: Old Keeper
has_key.text: Be careful what lies beyond. Not all doors are meant to be opened.

explored_crypt_02.speaker: Old Keeper
explored_crypt_02.text: You've seen the Bone Chamber and returned alive. That's more than most can say.

explored_crypt_02.speaker: Old Keeper
explored_crypt_02.text: The deeper you go, the darker it gets. But you already knew that.

asked_about_moss.speaker: Old Keeper
asked_about_moss.text: Bioluminescent moss? Aye, I know where it grows.

asked_about_moss.speaker: Old Keeper
asked_about_moss.text: Deep in the Bone Chamber — the second level of the crypt. Look along the far walls where the water seeps through.

asked_about_moss.speaker: Old Keeper
asked_about_moss.text: The moss feeds on the minerals in the runoff. It's the only living thing down there that doesn't want to kill you.

asked_about_moss.speaker: Old Keeper
asked_about_moss.text: Be careful harvesting it. Disturbing the moss sometimes attracts the skeletons. They guard everything in those depths.

has_watchtower_journal.speaker: Old Keeper
has_watchtower_journal.text: Where did you find this? The old watchtower... I thought it had collapsed years ago.

has_watchtower_journal.speaker: Old Keeper
has_watchtower_journal.text: I knew the man who wrote this journal. Watcher Corrin. He stayed at his post long after everyone else abandoned the perimeter.

has_watchtower_journal.speaker: Old Keeper
has_watchtower_journal.text: He documented the retreat of the light, year by year. Every failed floodlight. Every meter of ground we lost.

has_watchtower_journal.speaker: Old Keeper
has_watchtower_journal.text: 'The light went out.' That was his way. Never dramatic. Just... factual.

has_watchtower_journal.speaker: Old Keeper
has_watchtower_journal.text: He deserved better than to be forgotten up there. Thank you for bringing this to me.

dialogue.speaker: Warden Holt
dialogue.text: Welcome to Outpost Balor. We've been expecting you.

default.speaker: Warden Holt
default.text: Welcome to Outpost Balor. We've been expecting you.

default.speaker: Warden Holt
default.text: First things first — you need to be armed. Head to the munitions depot and see Quartermaster Voss.

default.speaker: Warden Holt
default.text: She'll set you up with a weapon. After that, report to the workshop — the engineer needs your help.

has_weapon.speaker: Warden Holt
has_weapon.text: Good, you're armed. The engineer in the workshop has your Sol Unit — almost finished, but he's run into a problem.

has_weapon.speaker: Warden Holt
has_weapon.text: Head through the east corridor. There are some supplies along the way. Help yourself.

quest_active.speaker: Warden Holt
quest_active.text: The engineer sent you into the occupied wing? Those luddites took it over weeks ago. We haven't had the manpower to clear them out.

quest_active.speaker: Warden Holt
quest_active.text: They're fanatics — hate anything tech. Watch yourself.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: Good. You made it back. Listen — I should tell you why you're really here.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: This planet is tidally locked. One side always faces the star, the other is in permanent darkness.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: We live on the border — the terminator zone. The only habitable strip on the whole world.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: The dark side isn't empty. The luddites operate out there. They reject the technology that keeps us alive and want to tear it all down.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: The lighthouses keep the border safe. A network of high-energy beacons that hold the line against raids from the dark side.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: We've lost contact with Lighthouse Mara. It went dark three days ago. The luddites are already pushing through the gap.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: You're being sent to repair it. That Sol Unit the engineer is finishing — you'll need it.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: Go talk to the engineer. Get your equipment. Then we move.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Warden Holt
has_sol_unit.text: You've got the Sol Unit. Good. But you're not ready yet.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Warden Holt
has_sol_unit.text: Talk to the people here. Learn what you can before heading out. The dark doesn't forgive ignorance.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Warden Holt
has_sol_unit.text: Check the mess hall — Surveyor Kade has maps of the route ahead. And if Tannis is conscious, get his report on the perimeter.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Warden Holt
has_sol_unit.text: The notice board in the mess hall has bounty postings too. Every bit of intel helps.

sol_unit_charged.speaker: Warden Holt
sol_unit_charged.text: Sol Unit's charged and ready. Good. You've done everything you can here.

sol_unit_charged.speaker: Warden Holt
sol_unit_charged.text: The perimeter gate is to the north. Beyond it, you're on your own — no more outpost walls, no more patrols.

sol_unit_charged.speaker: Warden Holt
sol_unit_charged.text: The dark perimeter is dangerous ground. Creatures out there are drawn to light, and your Sol Unit will be the brightest thing for kilometers.

sol_unit_charged.speaker: Warden Holt
sol_unit_charged.text: Follow the path to the train station. It's the only way to reach Meridian City — and from there, Lighthouse Mara.

sol_unit_charged.speaker: Warden Holt
sol_unit_charged.text: Good luck. We're all counting on you.

ready_to_leave.speaker: Warden Holt
ready_to_leave.text: You've talked to the right people. You're as ready as anyone can be.

ready_to_leave.speaker: Warden Holt
ready_to_leave.text: Lighthouse Mara is waiting. Don't let us down.

returned_from_meridian.speaker: Warden Holt
returned_from_meridian.text: You made it to Meridian and back. That makes you one of the few.

returned_from_meridian.speaker: Warden Holt
returned_from_meridian.text: Things have gotten worse here while you were gone. Perimeter activity has doubled — more creatures, bolder attacks. Something's pushing them toward us.

returned_from_meridian.speaker: Warden Holt
returned_from_meridian.text: I need you to scout a new area beyond the old perimeter line. Head west through the Dead Road — past where Tannis was attacked.

returned_from_meridian.speaker: Warden Holt
returned_from_meridian.text: The dark has crept closer. Whatever you find out there, report back.

has_fens_letter.speaker: Warden Holt
has_fens_letter.text: What's this? A letter addressed to me...

has_fens_letter.speaker: Warden Holt
has_fens_letter.text: Fen Maro. I wondered what happened to them. Lost their whole squad on a deep patrol, came back different.

has_fens_letter.speaker: Warden Holt
has_fens_letter.text: I filed them as missing when they stopped reporting. Didn't know they'd made it all the way to Meridian.

has_fens_letter.speaker: Warden Holt
has_fens_letter.text: Tell them... tell them I understand. And that there's always a place here if they want it.

has_fens_letter.speaker: Warden Holt
has_fens_letter.text: Their squad's supply cache — I know where it is. They stashed gear in a collapsed bunker northeast of the deep perimeter, past the old road.

has_fens_letter.speaker: Warden Holt
has_fens_letter.text: There was military-grade equipment in that cache. Mk1+ Sol Unit frame, hardened battery casings. If it's still intact, you should recover it.

letter_delivered.speaker: Warden Holt
letter_delivered.text: You delivered Fen's message. Thank you for that.

letter_delivered.speaker: Warden Holt
letter_delivered.text: The perimeter's still a mess. Those new creatures — Gloom Wraiths, the scouts are calling them — they attack from range. Be careful out there.

letter_delivered.speaker: Warden Holt
letter_delivered.text: If you haven't found Fen's cache yet, it's in a collapsed bunker northeast of the deep perimeter. Military-grade gear.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Warden Holt
has_resonance_fragment.text: What is that? The crystal in your pack — it's humming. I can feel it through the table.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Warden Holt
has_resonance_fragment.text: I've been doing this job for fifteen years, and I've never seen anything like that. Where did you find it?

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Warden Holt
has_resonance_fragment.text: The Underlumen... I always thought it was Unbounded superstition. But after what Daley's been picking up on comms, and now this...

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Warden Holt
has_resonance_fragment.text: Be careful who you show that to. The Council, the Array — they'll all want it. Make sure you know what you're giving away before you give it.

dialogue.speaker: Warden Holt
dialogue.text: I'll be checking on the perimeter. Talk to the engineer.

default.speaker: Warden Holt
default.text: I'll be checking on the perimeter. Talk to the engineer.

quest_active.speaker: Warden Holt
quest_active.text: Still here? The occupied wing is through the east corridor. Get moving.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: Good. You made it back. Listen — I should tell you why you're really here.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: This planet is tidally locked. One side always faces the star, the other is in permanent darkness.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: We live on the border — the terminator zone. The only habitable strip on the whole world.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: The dark side isn't empty. The luddites operate out there. They reject the technology that keeps us alive and want to tear it all down.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: The lighthouses keep the border safe. A network of high-energy beacons that hold the line against raids from the dark side.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: You're being sent to repair it. That Sol Unit the engineer is finishing — you'll need it.

has_cylinders.speaker: Warden Holt
has_cylinders.text: Go talk to the engineer. Get your equipment. Then we move.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Warden Holt
has_sol_unit.text: You've got the Sol Unit. Good.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Warden Holt
has_sol_unit.text: Lighthouse Mara is waiting. Don't let us down.

dialogue.speaker: Guard Patel
dialogue.text: At ease. Warden's been expecting someone.

default.speaker: Guard Patel
default.text: At ease. Warden's been expecting someone. Check in with him before you do anything else.

default.speaker: Guard Patel
default.text: This outpost runs on schedule. You're either on duty, in the racks, or at the mess.

default.speaker: Guard Patel
default.text: Dark side's been quiet the last two cycles. That's usually when you should start worrying.

quest_active.speaker: Guard Patel
quest_active.text: The occupied wing is no place to be wandering. Watch yourself in there.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Guard Patel
has_sol_unit.text: Heard you cleared the occupied wing. That was either brave or stupid.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Guard Patel
has_sol_unit.text: Either way — good work.

dialogue.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
dialogue.text: Six months on Balor rotation. Two to go — if relief ever shows.

default.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
default.text: Six months on Balor rotation. Two to go — if relief ever shows.

default.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
default.text: We pushed a luddite scouting party back to grid seven last week. Three of them, none of us. Good day.

default.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
default.text: They're fanatics, but they're not stupid. When your tech is on your hip, they know it.

quest_active.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
quest_active.text: They've been camped in the east wing for weeks. We didn't have the numbers to clear them.

quest_active.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
quest_active.text: Stay low, move fast. They'll try to smash your gear before they try to smash you.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Cpl. Reyes
has_sol_unit.text: Nice kit. Engineer does good work when he's got the parts.

default.speaker: Pvt. Dunnmore
default.text: Trouble sleeping. The dark side makes noise on the sensors — not enough to trigger alert, just enough to keep you up.

default.speaker: Pvt. Dunnmore
default.text: I signed up because I believed in the lighthouse network. Didn't think I'd spend six months staring at walls.

default.speaker: Pvt. Dunnmore
default.text: My family lives in Sector Nine. Right on the border line. If the beacons fail out there...

default.speaker: Pvt. Dunnmore
default.text: Just — don't let the beacons fail.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Pvt. Dunnmore
has_sol_unit.text: You're heading to Lighthouse Mara?

has_sol_unit.speaker: Pvt. Dunnmore
has_sol_unit.text: Get it back online. Please.

dialogue.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
dialogue.text: I've been on the terminator line for thirty years. I know what a failing grid looks like.

default.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
default.text: I've been on the terminator line since before Lighthouse Mara was commissioned. Thirty years on this rock.

default.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
default.text: The lighthouses don't just push back raids. They keep the whole border stable — settlements, crops, water reclamation, all of it runs on that grid.

default.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
default.text: Mara going dark isn't just a tactical problem. It's a crack in everything. And cracks spread.

quest_active.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
quest_active.text: Engineer sent you into the occupied wing? Good. We've let that fester long enough.

quest_active.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
quest_active.text: Watch for the warlord at the back. He's not like the others — he plans.

has_cylinders.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
has_cylinders.text: You found the cylinders. Take them to the engineer and get your Sol Unit sorted.

has_cylinders.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
has_cylinders.text: Every hour that lighthouse is dark is another hour the luddites push through the gap.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
has_sol_unit.text: Sol Unit's ready. Good. Get to Lighthouse Mara before the luddites fortify the approach.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Sgt. Ellers
has_sol_unit.text: And come back in one piece. We're short on people as it is.

dialogue.speaker: Tech Maren
dialogue.text: The capacitor banks are up. Don't touch the terminals without clearance.

default.speaker: Tech Maren
default.text: This is the main capacitor bank. Solar collectors on the outer hull run continuous collection along the terminator — the light out here never stops.

default.speaker: Tech Maren
default.text: Devices that run on Sol energy — Sol Units, light rifles, beacon relay cores — can all be charged at the interface terminals. Third slot from the left.

default.speaker: Tech Maren
default.text: We're still calibrating the output profiles. The system isn't fully certified yet, but it's stable enough.

default.speaker: Tech Maren
default.text: When you get a Sol Unit, bring it in. Once we're fully online, a charge cycle takes minutes.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: Sol Unit's nearly drained? Yeah, I can see the output readings from here. Slot it in — third terminal from the left.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: ...There. Charge cycle complete. You're at full capacity.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: You should know — this generator is the single most valuable piece of equipment at Outpost Balor. Maybe on this whole stretch of the terminator.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: Erith is tidally locked. Permanent day on one hemisphere, permanent night on the other. We live on the terminator — the thin strip between the two.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: The only scalable power source on the planet is solar, and all of it comes from the dayside. Every watt that reaches the nightside comes through the lighthouse relay network.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: On the nightside? Batteries and portable generators. Both expensive. Both limited. If the supply lines from the dayside ever get cut...

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: The other option is uranium, mined off-planet. But the shipping costs make it a luxury. Only the core settlements can afford reactor fuel.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: So this generator — and the lighthouse network that powers it — that's what keeps every Sol Unit, every light rifle, every outpost on the terminator running.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: Lighthouse Mara going dark isn't just a security problem. It's an energy problem. Without that relay, this whole sector loses its power feed.

needs_charge.speaker: Tech Maren
needs_charge.text: Keep your unit charged. And keep those lighthouses running. Everything depends on it.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Tech Maren
has_sol_unit.text: You've got a Sol Unit? Good. Third slot from the left — connect the interface and I'll run the charge sequence.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Tech Maren
has_sol_unit.text: We're not fully certified yet, so the output's capped. But it'll top you off before a deployment.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Tech Maren
has_sol_unit.text: Come back when you've run it down. That's what we're here for.

charged.speaker: Tech Maren
charged.text: Unit's fully charged. Come back when you need a top-up — that's what we're here for.

charged.speaker: Tech Maren
charged.text: And remember — out in the field, you won't have a charging terminal. Manage your energy carefully.

dialogue.speaker: Guard Pell
dialogue.text: Power room's access-restricted.

default.speaker: Guard Pell
default.text: Power room's access-restricted. Tech Maren's the only one authorized to touch those consoles.

default.speaker: Guard Pell
default.text: You need a charge, you talk to her.

dialogue.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
dialogue.text: Everything in this depot is catalogued. You requisition, you sign, you return.

has_weapon.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
has_weapon.text: Good choice. The workshop's back through the main hall — east corridor. Engineer's been waiting.

has_weapon.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
has_weapon.text: Medical supplies are stocked by my station. Take what you need and log it.

quest_active.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
quest_active.text: Heading into the occupied wing? I've got a job for you.

quest_active.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
quest_active.text: Two weeks back, luddites hit the east supply run. We lost three crates of class-four cells and a case of light rifle packs.

quest_active.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
quest_active.text: The cargo's gone, but the supply manifest should still be there. It was clipped to the lead crate.

quest_active.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
quest_active.text: I need it back so I can file for replacements. Should be somewhere in the outer corridor — look near the storage alcoves.

quest_active.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
quest_active.text: Take the bandages on the way out. Don't be a hero about resupply.

side_quest_active.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
side_quest_active.text: Any luck with that supply manifest? Should be in the outer corridor of the occupied wing, near the storage alcoves.

side_quest_has_manifest.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
side_quest_has_manifest.text: You found it! Let me see...

side_quest_has_manifest.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
side_quest_has_manifest.text: Class-four cells, light rifle packs, field rations... worse than I thought. But at least now I can file the requisition.

side_quest_has_manifest.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
side_quest_has_manifest.text: Good work. Take these — you'll need them more than the depot does.

side_quest_complete.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
side_quest_complete.text: Replacement requisition is filed. Command will take their time, as usual.

side_quest_complete.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
side_quest_complete.text: At least we know what we're short on now. Thanks again.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Quartermaster Voss
has_sol_unit.text: Sol Unit's charged and ready? Good. Watch the east corridor on the way to Mara — that route's been compromised.

dialogue.speaker: Pvt. Korrin
dialogue.text: These light rifles haven't been serviced in eight weeks.

default.speaker: Pvt. Korrin
default.text: Six light rifles in here haven't been serviced in eight weeks. Quartermaster says no time. I say that's how you get a misfire.

default.speaker: Pvt. Korrin
default.text: Everything on this rock runs on Sol energy. The lighthouses, the weapons, the outpost grid.

default.speaker: Pvt. Korrin
default.text: The beacons go down, we lose power too — eventually. Not right away, but it cascades.

dialogue.speaker: Tech Yara
dialogue.text: Charging terminal's active. Bring your Sol Unit over.

default.speaker: Tech Yara
default.text: Wait — is that a person? An actual human being?

default.speaker: Tech Yara
default.text: Sorry, it's just — I haven't seen another person in weeks. The last patrol from Balor was over a month ago.

default.speaker: Tech Yara
default.text: I'm Yara. Station tech. I keep the transit systems operational, though 'operational' is a strong word these days.

default.speaker: Tech Yara
default.text: The train to Meridian City still runs — automated, on a fixed schedule. But I can't authorize passengers without a Transit Pass.

default.speaker: Tech Yara
default.text: Problem is, something's wrong with Junction Box 7 outside. It's been making terrible noises. Grinding, screeching. I haven't dared check it alone.

default.speaker: Tech Yara
default.text: Clear whatever's nesting out there and I'll authorize your Transit Pass. Fair deal?

junction_quest_active.speaker: Tech Yara
junction_quest_active.text: The junction box is through the east door. Just... be careful out there. Whatever moved in, it's been getting louder.

junction_cleared.speaker: Tech Yara
junction_cleared.text: You cleared it? Oh thank the light. I've been hearing those sounds for days.

junction_cleared.speaker: Tech Yara
junction_cleared.text: A deal's a deal. Here's your Transit Pass — authorized for one trip to Meridian City.

junction_cleared.speaker: Tech Yara
junction_cleared.text: The train's automated. Just open the platform gate at the north end of the station and step on. MERIDIAN-7 handles the rest.

junction_cleared.speaker: Tech Yara
junction_cleared.text: Oh, and if you're looking to trade in the city, there's a merchant named Volkov who buys relics and salvage. Pays well for pre-dark stuff.

has_transit_pass.speaker: Tech Yara
has_transit_pass.text: You've got your pass. The platform gate is at the north end of the station.

has_transit_pass.speaker: Tech Yara
has_transit_pass.text: Meridian City is... well, it's something. Biggest settlement in the terminator zone. You'll be safe there. Mostly.

has_transit_pass.speaker: Tech Yara
has_transit_pass.text: Tell them Yara sent you if anyone gives you trouble at the gates.

has_charged.speaker: Tech Yara
has_charged.text: Unit's topped off. You're good to go.

has_charged.speaker: Tech Yara
has_charged.text: Come back whenever you need a recharge. That's what I'm here for.

dialogue.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
dialogue.text: // SOLAR TERMINAL ACTIVE // AWAITING INPUT //

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: // SOLAR TERMINAL ACTIVE // DESIGNATION: MERIDIAN-7 // ARRAY TRADE INTERFACE //

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: I am the Array's liaison for this sector. My function is resource exchange and infrastructure coordination.

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: The dayside is automated. Harvesters collect silicon. Solar panels generate power. The Array manages all of it.

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: Humans cannot survive on the dayside without protection. But you can deploy structures remotely through this terminal.

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: The Array requires umbracite — a rare crystalline mineral found in the terminator zone. Bring me umbracite and I will provide infrastructure in return.

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: There may be a fragment nearby. This station was once a transit hub — materials pass through here.

has_umbracite.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_umbracite.text: You have umbracite. The Array values this mineral above all others. It is essential to our expansion protocols.

has_umbracite.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_umbracite.text: I will deploy a Solar Panel on the dayside in exchange. It will passively recharge your Sol Unit while you are there.

has_umbracite.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_umbracite.text: Interact again to confirm the exchange.

traded.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
traded.text: Your solar panel is active on the dayside. It will recharge your Sol Unit passively while you are in the solar fields.

traded.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
traded.text: Silicon is abundant on the dayside. Collect it to build more structures through your AUTO interface.

traded.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
traded.text: When you have surplus silicon, return here. I can offer equipment, components, and advanced schematics in exchange.

returning.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
returning.text: Your dayside structures continue to produce while you are away. Let me show you the current status.

returning.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
returning.text: The Array values consistent trade partners. Continue building and we will both benefit.

dialogue.speaker: Cook Brannigan
dialogue.text: Kitchen's open. Grab a tray and sit down.

default.speaker: Cook Brannigan
default.text: Twelve years I've been feeding this outpost. Twelve years of the same ration slop, and not one complaint I care about.

default.speaker: Cook Brannigan
default.text: Everyone talks in the mess hall. I hear things. You need to know what's going on around here, you come talk to me.

default.speaker: Cook Brannigan
default.text: Grab a ration pack if you're hungry. They taste like cardboard, but they'll keep you standing.

rations_missing.speaker: Cook Brannigan
rations_missing.text: Listen, I've got a problem. Someone's been stealing rations from the supply closet.

rations_missing.speaker: Cook Brannigan
rations_missing.text: Three packs last week, five this week. I've counted twice. It's not rats — we don't have rats.

rations_missing.speaker: Cook Brannigan
rations_missing.text: I think someone's sneaking in after hours. If you're poking around the outpost, keep your eyes open.

rations_missing.speaker: Cook Brannigan
rations_missing.text: Check the storage area here for scratch marks. And the workshop — that's where I'd hide if I didn't want to be found.

found_note.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_note.text: You found a note? In the workshop? Let me see that.

found_note.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_note.text: 'Hold out until the next train...' So someone was hiding down there. Living off my rations.

found_note.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_note.text: A deserter, maybe. Or a refugee from one of the border settlements. Either way, they're gone now.

found_note.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_note.text: Check the basement if you can get down there. Might be something useful left behind.

found_basement.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_basement.text: So there really was someone down there. Living under our feet the whole time.

found_basement.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_basement.text: A journal fragment? 'Catching the train to Meridian...' Whoever it was, they made it out. Probably.

found_basement.speaker: Cook Brannigan
found_basement.text: Here — take these. Consider it thanks for solving my mystery. And if you ever pass through Meridian City, keep an eye out for our ghost.

quest_complete.speaker: Cook Brannigan
quest_complete.text: Mystery's solved. Rations are accounted for. Things are back to normal.

quest_complete.speaker: Cook Brannigan
quest_complete.text: You know, whoever was hiding down there... I hope they made it. The border's no place to be alone.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Cook Brannigan
has_sol_unit.text: Sol Unit, huh? Means you're heading out soon.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Cook Brannigan
has_sol_unit.text: I've seen a lot of people leave through that north gate. Not all of them come back.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Cook Brannigan
has_sol_unit.text: Eat before you go. Trust me on that.

dialogue.speaker: Pvt. Osei
dialogue.text: Is it true? About the dark side? That nothing comes back?

default.speaker: Pvt. Osei
default.text: I just got posted here three weeks ago. They didn't tell us much in training — just 'hold the line' and 'don't go past the perimeter alone.'

default.speaker: Pvt. Osei
default.text: Is it true what they say about the Nightside? That there are things out there that don't need light to see?

default.speaker: Pvt. Osei
default.text: Sgt. Ellers says the dark isn't empty. He says it's full. That's what scares me.

default.speaker: Pvt. Osei
default.text: I signed up to protect people. I just... didn't think it would be this quiet. The waiting is worse than the fighting.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Pvt. Osei
has_sol_unit.text: You have a Sol Unit? Those are rare — I've only seen pictures in the manual.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Pvt. Osei
has_sol_unit.text: How does it feel? Does it really push back the dark?

has_sol_unit.speaker: Pvt. Osei
has_sol_unit.text: I wish I had one. Maybe then I wouldn't be scared of patrol duty.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Pvt. Osei
has_sol_unit.text: Be careful out there. And... come back, okay? Morale's bad enough as it is.

dialogue.speaker: Surveyor Kade
dialogue.text: Mind the maps. They're not finished.

default.speaker: Surveyor Kade
default.text: I'm a civilian cartographer — attached to the outpost for the survey season. Mapping the terminator zone between here and the train station.

default.speaker: Surveyor Kade
default.text: The terrain shifts constantly out there. The temperature gradient at the terminator creates geological instability. Paths that existed last month are gone.

default.speaker: Surveyor Kade
default.text: If you're heading through the perimeter, I can mark what I know on your HUD. There are side routes that avoid the main luddite patrol lanes.

default.speaker: Surveyor Kade
default.text: Just promise me you'll report back what you see. I need ground truth for the survey.

intel_given.speaker: Surveyor Kade
intel_given.text: I've shared what I know. The marked paths should help you avoid the worst of it.

intel_given.speaker: Surveyor Kade
intel_given.text: Remember — the dark side erodes landmarks. Don't trust anything that looks too familiar.

dialogue.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
dialogue.text: Long-range comms are down. All I'm getting is static.

default.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
default.text: This is the comms room. Or what's left of it.

default.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
default.text: The long-range radio took damage in the last luddite push. I can manage local frequencies, but anything beyond twenty klicks is dead.

default.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
default.text: I need two things to get it running: a relay circuit board and a backup power cell. The circuit board might be in the old supply caches — try the crypts. The power cell... somewhere on the perimeter, I think.

default.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
default.text: If you come across either, bring them to me. We need to know what's happening at the other outposts.

has_circuit_board.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_circuit_board.text: A circuit board! Let me see — yes, this is the right relay type. Good condition too.

has_circuit_board.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_circuit_board.text: I still need a backup power cell to complete the repair. Check the perimeter — there should be emergency supply caches out there.

has_power_cell.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_power_cell.text: A power cell! That's one of the two things I need.

has_power_cell.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_power_cell.text: I still need a relay circuit board. The old crypts might have supply caches with compatible parts.

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: You've got both parts? Give me a minute...

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: ...Circuit board seated. Power cell connected. Frequency calibration...

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: We're getting signal! Weak, but it's there. I'm picking up fragments from Outpost Duskwall.

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: '...situation critical... lighthouse array failing... request immediate...' — then it cuts out.

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: This is bad. Duskwall is three sectors over. If their lighthouses are failing too, this isn't a local problem.

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: There's another signal on an unregistered frequency. Someone calling themselves 'Sable.' Never heard that callsign before.

has_both_parts.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_both_parts.text: Take this — a Signal Booster chip I had stashed for the repair. You'll need it more than I will now.

comms_restored.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
comms_restored.text: Comms are up — partially. I'm monitoring all frequencies.

comms_restored.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
comms_restored.text: Duskwall's transmissions are getting worse. They're talking about evacuating the outer settlements.

comms_restored.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
comms_restored.text: And that 'Sable' signal keeps appearing. Whoever they are, they're using Unbounded encryption. That's... unusual.

comms_restored.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
comms_restored.text: I'll keep listening. If I pick up anything urgent, I'll pass it along.

new_signal.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
new_signal.text: You're back from Meridian? Good timing. I've intercepted something new.

new_signal.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
new_signal.text: A distorted voice, repeating coordinates on loop. Not Duskwall's frequency — this is older. Much older.

new_signal.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
new_signal.text: The signal's been broadcasting for years, maybe decades. We only picked it up because the comms upgrade improved our range.

new_signal.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
new_signal.text: The coordinates point to a location deep in the perimeter — west of the Dead Road, somewhere underground.

new_signal.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
new_signal.text: Here — I've written them down. Find the signal source. Someone out there has been calling for help for a very long time.

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: You found the source? A dead Lightkeeper...

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: Let me see that journal. Yes — I can cross-reference the ID against our records.

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: Lightkeeper Renn Cavari. Filed as 'missing, presumed lost' fourteen years ago. Deep patrol, never reported back.

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: At least now we know. I'll log them as KIA and close the file. Their family deserves to know.

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: The route data from Cavari's transmitter is interesting. They mapped a path deeper into the Nightside than any official survey.

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: I'm adding it to your map data. When you're ready to go further into the dark... Cavari already blazed the trail.

signal_found.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
signal_found.text: Also — there's been increasing chatter about Luddite activity along the Lighthouse network. Whatever's happening out there, it's getting bigger.

has_relay_log.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_relay_log.text: A relay operations log? Let me see that.

has_relay_log.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_relay_log.text: This is from Relay Station 7 — it went dark about six years ago. We always assumed it was equipment failure.

has_relay_log.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_relay_log.text: But this last entry... 'Something moving under the ground. Seismic readings off the chart. Coordinates don't match any settlement.'

has_relay_log.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_relay_log.text: That matches some anomalous readings I've been picking up on the restored frequencies. Deep-earth vibrations. Rhythmic, almost... purposeful.

has_relay_log.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_relay_log.text: The Underlumen. It's an old Unbounded legend — something that lives beneath the dark side. Most people think it's superstition.

has_relay_log.speaker: Comms Officer Daley
has_relay_log.text: But if this relay operator was detecting the same thing six years ago... maybe it's not just a legend.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Vasik
dialogue.text: Infirmary's full. What do you need?

default.speaker: Dr. Vasik
default.text: Dr. Lira Vasik. I'm the only medic at Outpost Balor, which means I'm permanently overworked.

default.speaker: Dr. Vasik
default.text: I've got a wounded soldier — Pvt. Tannis. Something got him on the perimeter. Deep lacerations, possible toxin.

default.speaker: Dr. Vasik
default.text: I need bioluminescent moss for a healing salve. It grows in the deep crypts, but nobody here knows where to find it.

default.speaker: Dr. Vasik
default.text: The Old Keeper in the crypt — if anyone knows where that moss grows, it's him. Talk to him for me?

keeper_told.speaker: Dr. Vasik
keeper_told.text: The Old Keeper told you where to find the moss? Good. It should be deeper in the crypt — the Bone Chamber.

keeper_told.speaker: Dr. Vasik
keeper_told.text: Bring it back as soon as you can. Tannis doesn't have a lot of time.

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: You found it! Let me see...

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: Perfect. Bioluminescent moss, fresh and viable. I can work with this.

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: Give me a moment to prepare the salve...

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: There. Tannis will pull through. It'll take time, but the infection's neutralized.

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: You know, the Array would have us use synthetic compounds for everything. But organic remedies like this — they work with the body, not against it.

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: Here — I'll show you how to make Field Medkits. Same principle as the salve, scaled for field use. Much better than standard bandages.

has_moss.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_moss.text: You should be able to find the materials you need in supply caches and the crypts.

quest_complete.speaker: Dr. Vasik
quest_complete.text: Tannis is recovering well. He's been asking about you.

quest_complete.speaker: Dr. Vasik
quest_complete.text: The Array's medical tech is impressive, I'll give them that. But I don't trust anything that requires a network connection to diagnose a broken bone.

quest_complete.speaker: Dr. Vasik
quest_complete.text: Stay safe out there. And if you get hurt, use those medkits I taught you about.

has_bio_samples.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_bio_samples.text: Are those biological samples? Let me see...

has_bio_samples.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_bio_samples.text: Remarkable. These organisms are producing compounds I've never seen before. The bioluminescence isn't just light — it's a chemical signature.

has_bio_samples.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_bio_samples.text: If you're taking these to someone for research, let me prepare proper preservation compounds. Unpreserved specimens degrade within hours.

has_bio_samples.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_bio_samples.text: There — properly sealed and temperature-stabilized. The cellular structure will hold for weeks now.

has_bio_samples.speaker: Dr. Vasik
has_bio_samples.text: Whoever gets these will owe you. And me.

dialogue.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
dialogue.text: *coughs* ...who...

default.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
default.text: *coughs weakly* Something... got me on the perimeter. Fast. Small. Came in packs.

default.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
default.text: Never seen anything like them before. Insect-like. Moved low to the ground.

default.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
default.text: The dark's getting closer. I could feel it... pressing against the outpost walls.

default.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
default.text: Doc says I need some kind of moss... from the crypt. Please... hurry.

recovering.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
recovering.text: The salve is working. I can feel it. Doc Vasik knows her stuff.

recovering.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
recovering.text: Listen — before you head out to the perimeter, you should know what's out there.

recovering.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
recovering.text: The crawlers — they're new. They weren't there a month ago. They're scouts for something bigger.

recovering.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
recovering.text: They move fast and they swarm. Don't let them surround you. And watch the edges of the light — that's where they hide.

recovering.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
recovering.text: The perimeter isn't safe anymore. Whatever's happening with the lighthouses... it's making the dark bolder.

has_dog_tags.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
has_dog_tags.text: My dog tags... you found them out there?

has_dog_tags.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
has_dog_tags.text: I lost them when those things dragged me. I thought I'd never... I mean, they're just tags, but...

has_dog_tags.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
has_dog_tags.text: My squad — the three of us who were on perimeter patrol that night. Cpl. Meyrin and Spc. Dolan didn't make it back.

has_dog_tags.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
has_dog_tags.text: I was the only one. I don't know why. Maybe because I was closest to the wall when they hit.

has_dog_tags.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
has_dog_tags.text: Thank you. I want you to have this — it was Dolan's. He modified the battery casing himself. Good engineer.

has_dog_tags.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
has_dog_tags.text: Take it. Use it. Make sure what happened to my squad means something.

light_duty.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
light_duty.text: I'm on light duty now. Gate watch. Not exactly thrilling, but at least I'm up and moving.

light_duty.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
light_duty.text: Listen — you're heading deeper into the perimeter, right? I need to tell you something.

light_duty.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
light_duty.text: There's a ravine to the northwest, past the old road. We lost three people there on a deep patrol last year.

light_duty.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
light_duty.text: But there's something in it — I saw lights. Not our lights. Not flares, not equipment. Something growing on the walls.

light_duty.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
light_duty.text: The things that live down there are bigger than anything near the outpost. Armored. Deliberate. We called them Lurkers.

light_duty.speaker: Pvt. Tannis
light_duty.text: Be careful. And if you find what's making those lights... let me know. I've been wondering about them since.

dialogue.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
dialogue.text: You must be here for the Sol Unit. I've got bad news.

first_meeting.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
first_meeting.text: You must be here for the Sol Unit. I've got bad news.

first_meeting.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
first_meeting.text: The repairs are almost done, but I'm missing critical parts. Titanium power cylinders — I can't finish without them.

first_meeting.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
first_meeting.text: There's a supply cache in the east wing. Problem is, luddites seized that section. They've been camped there for weeks.

first_meeting.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
first_meeting.text: The cylinders should still be in the cache, unless those wreckers have smashed them already.

first_meeting.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
first_meeting.text: I know it's a lot to ask, but I can't leave the shop. The Unit's in a delicate state. Can you get them for me?

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: You must be here for the Sol Unit. I've got bad news.

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: The repairs are almost done, but I'm missing critical parts. Titanium power cylinders — I can't finish without them.

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: There's a supply cache in the east wing. Problem is, luddites seized that section. They've been camped there for weeks.

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: The cylinders should still be in the cache, unless those wreckers have smashed them already.

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: I know it's a lot to ask, but I can't leave the shop. The Unit's in a delicate state. Can you get them for me?

quest_active.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
quest_active.text: The occupied wing is through the east corridor. The cylinders should be in the supply cache at the far end.

quest_active.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
quest_active.text: Be careful. Those luddites don't take kindly to anyone carrying tech.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: You found them! Let me see... yes, perfect. Undamaged.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: Give me just a moment...

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: There — your Sol Unit's ready. Channels concentrated solar energy. She'll keep you alive out there.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: I've mounted a Sol Cone emitter in the center — that's your main attack.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: Here, take this Damage Booster chip too. It's a modifier — slot it next to the Sol Cone to power it up.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: Press [I] to open your Inventory, click OPEN on your weapon slot, and drag the booster next to the Sol Cone. Talk to me when you're done.

slot_booster_reminder.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
slot_booster_reminder.text: Open your Inventory with [I], click OPEN on your weapon slot, and drag the Damage Booster next to the Sol Cone.

slot_booster_reminder.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
slot_booster_reminder.text: Come talk to me once it's in place.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: Feel the difference? Adjacent modifiers power up nearby abilities — that's how you build.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: As you find more components, think about what goes next to what. Grid placement is everything.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: One more thing — energy is precious out here. Every shot costs power, and recharging isn't easy.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: Head south to the training range. Put a few rounds downrange, then see Tech Maren at the Power Station to recharge.

go_train.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
go_train.text: The training range is through the south door. Go put a few rounds downrange — get a feel for the Sol Beam.

go_train.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
go_train.text: Energy's hard to come by, so don't waste it. But you've got enough for some training — hit the Power Station afterward to recharge.

training_done.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
training_done.text: Nice shooting. The Sol Beam packs a punch, doesn't it?

training_done.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
training_done.text: But you're running on fumes now. Head to the Power Station — south exit from the main hall. Tech Maren will get you charged up.

training_done.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
training_done.text: That generator is the most important thing in this outpost. Without it, every Sol Unit and light rifle on the base goes dark.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_sol_unit.text: That Sol Unit is solid work, if I say so myself. Take care of it and it'll take care of you.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_sol_unit.text: When you get back, I might be able to upgrade it. If you bring me the right materials.

dialogue.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
dialogue.text: Hold up. This gate doesn't open without my say-so.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Gate Sergeant Fenn. Twenty years on the perimeter.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: So you're the one Holt is sending out there. Can't say I envy you.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Every year the dark gets a little closer. Every year we pull the line back a little more.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Used to be you could see the old watchtower from here. Now it's swallowed up. Nothing but dark past this gate.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Here — take this flare. Standard issue for perimeter crossings. Save it for when you really need it.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Stay on the main road if you can. The crawlers are bad, but the Shade Stalkers are worse. Fast, smart, and they hunt in pairs.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: I'm opening the gate. Once it closes behind you... well, there's no coming back through this way.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Good luck out there. You'll need it.

gate_opened.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
gate_opened.text: Gate's open. Head north through the outer ring.

gate_opened.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
gate_opened.text: Remember — Shade Stalkers hunt in pairs. Keep your Sol Unit charged and your eyes open.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: Please — don't shoot.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: Please — don't shoot. I'm not a raider. I'm not Unbounded — well, I am, but not the kind you're thinking of.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: My name is Sable. I came from the deep Nightside to warn the Ring settlements.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: Something is stirring out there. Something beneath the dark. The ground itself is... moving.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The Unbounded aren't all raiders. We have settlements — hidden ones, with bioluminescent gardens. We live with the dark, not against it.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: But whatever's happening down below is driving the creatures to the surface. The Shade Stalkers, the crawlers — they're fleeing from something worse.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: I've been hiding behind this wreck, waiting for those stalkers to move on. Thank you for driving them off.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: If you're heading to the train station, I'll walk with you. I can teach you to read the dark — the signs, the trails.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The Unbounded leave markers. Small things — scratches on walls, patterns in debris. They mark safe passages and warnings.

helped.speaker: Sable
helped.text: We should keep moving. The stalkers in this area won't stay scared for long.

helped.speaker: Sable
helped.text: You fight well, by the way. Most Ring soldiers shoot first and ask questions... well, they don't ask questions.

helped.speaker: Sable
helped.text: I need to reach Meridian City. There are people there who might listen. The Ring's council needs to know what's coming.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: You've been to the Dayside. I can smell the ozone on you — that scorched-glass stink.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: The Unbounded have stories about the light side. The elders call it the Furnace. They say the machines there never sleep, never stop building.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: My grandmother's grandmother watched the first solar arrays go up. By the time her children were grown, the arrays had doubled. Then doubled again.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: The Array gives you energy. It gives you equipment. But have you asked yourself what it's building when you're not looking?

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: The Unbounded left the Ring because they saw the pattern. Dependence becomes control. Control becomes... something else.

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: You made it to Meridian and came back here? The dark road is no place for nostalgia.

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: I suppose you've seen the city now. The lights, the markets, the Council's propaganda posters on every wall.

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: Did they tell you about the Unbounded? The official version — savages in the dark, raiders who destroy what they can't understand?

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: There's another version. One where we left because we understood too well.

post_array_secret.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret.text: You've been inside the Array. I can tell — you have that look. Like something you believed just broke.

post_array_secret.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret.text: The Unbounded knew. We always knew. That's why my people walked into the dark.

post_array_secret.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret.text: Find me in Meridian. My garden, near the residential quarter. We need to talk about what comes next.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: Almost there. I can see the station lights ahead.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: See those markings on the wall? Unbounded trail signs. This area is known to my people.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: That symbol — the broken circle — means 'settlement nearby.' Someone from the deep Nightside came through here before me.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The dead crawlers near the entrance... something killed them recently. Something bigger than a stalker.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The dark has its own ecosystem. We Unbounded have studied it for generations. But lately, even we can't predict what's coming next.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: The train station. I've heard stories about this place.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: This is where I leave you.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: I have my own way of traveling. The dark roads — paths through the Nightside that the Ring doesn't know about.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: I'll find you in Meridian City. There's a market district near the inner wall. Ask around for 'the dark woman' — people will point you to me.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: And... thank you. For helping me back there. For not shooting first.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: When we meet again, I'll teach you more about the Nightside. There are things out there worth protecting, not just fearing.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: *winces* ...You. I saw you on the road. You walked right past me.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: Don't worry — I'm not angry. I understand. Out here, trust is a luxury.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: I fought my way clear eventually. The stalkers got a few good hits in, but I'm tougher than I look.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: My name is Sable. I'm Unbounded — not a raider, before you reach for your weapon.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: I'm heading to Meridian City to warn the Ring about something stirring in the deep Nightside. That's all I'll say for now.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: Maybe in the city, if you're willing to listen, I'll tell you more. But trust has to be earned.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The train station. A crossroads. Even the Unbounded use the railways sometimes — in secret, of course.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: I'll be heading to Meridian City by my own route. The dark roads are faster, if you know the way.

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: You again. And you reek of solar radiation. You've been to the Furnace.

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: The Unbounded have a saying: 'The light that never sets casts the longest shadow.'

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: The Array showed you its fields, its harvesters, its generosity. Did it show you what lies behind the second wall? The structures it doesn't let humans inspect?

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: My people have watched the Dayside from the dark for generations. We see the glow on the horizon grow brighter every decade.

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: Ask MERIDIAN-7 what it's building. See if it gives you a straight answer.

post_dayside_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_not_helped.text: Back from the Dayside, are you? The machines treat you well, I'm sure.

post_dayside_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_not_helped.text: The Array is very good at making friends. Very patient. It thinks in centuries.

post_dayside_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_not_helped.text: I wonder — did it ask you about the Nightside? About what minerals you've found? It always asks.

post_meridian_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_helped.text: You came back to the station? Meridian not to your liking?

post_meridian_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_helped.text: I've been through the city already. The dark roads are fast. I have a garden now, near the residential quarter.

post_meridian_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_helped.text: Find me there when you're ready to hear what I really came to say. Some things shouldn't be spoken in a place this exposed.

post_meridian_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_not_helped.text: Still here? I thought you'd be enjoying the comforts of Meridian by now.

post_meridian_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_not_helped.text: I got to the city on my own. Took some scars with me, but the Unbounded are used to that.

post_meridian_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_not_helped.text: If you ever decide you want the truth about what's happening beneath the Nightside, you know where to find me.

post_array_secret_station.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret_station.text: The Array showed you what it's really doing, didn't it? The synthesis labs. The biological research.

post_array_secret_station.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret_station.text: Come find me in Meridian. The garden district. This isn't a conversation for a train platform.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Calloway
dialogue.text: Welcome to Meridian City.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: Welcome to Meridian City, traveler. You've come from the frontier, I can tell. That look in your eyes — everyone who crosses the dark has it.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: The city's divided into districts. Head north through the main concourse for the Market Quarter — supplies, weapons, components, everything you need.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: East corridor leads to the Civic Center — land registration, government offices. If you're claiming a salvage lot, that's where you go.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: West takes you to the Workshop District. Crafters, engineers, practical folk.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: The directory board on the wall has a full listing if you need it. Safe travels.

returning.speaker: Station Master Calloway
returning.text: Back again? The trains run on schedule now, thanks to the Array's timetable systems.

returning.speaker: Station Master Calloway
returning.text: Need directions? Market north, Civic east, Workshop west. Same as always.

courier_asked.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_asked.text: Halden? Yeah, I know him. Transit courier, ran the evening manifests. Quiet kid, kept his head down.

courier_asked.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_asked.text: Hasn't been at his post in days, though. Last time I saw him, he was in the Market Quarter — acting jumpy, looking over his shoulder. Left his logbook on the platform bench, if you can believe it.

courier_asked.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_asked.text: I put it aside for him, but he never came back for it. Might've ended up in the market — things get swept that way during the evening rush.

courier_done.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_done.text: Heard they found out what Halden was up to. Smuggling, of all things. In my station.

courier_done.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_done.text: Good riddance, I say. I run a clean operation here.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant Reva
dialogue.text: Fresh stock, fair prices.

default.speaker: Merchant Reva
default.text: Welcome, welcome! Reva's General Goods — everything a frontier traveler needs. Potions, bandages, rations, and more.

default.speaker: Merchant Reva
default.text: You look like you've been through it. Let me guess — Outpost Balor? The perimeter?

default.speaker: Merchant Reva
default.text: Well, you're in the right place. What can I get you?

has_relay_log.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_relay_log.text: Hold on — is that a relay log? Those are rare finds. The old lighthouse records.

has_relay_log.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_relay_log.text: I've got a regular customer who'd pay well for that. Archivist Solen, over in the Archives district. He's obsessed with pre-settlement history.

has_relay_log.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_relay_log.text: Tell him Reva sent you. He'll make it worth your while.

has_chitin.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_chitin.text: Is that chitin plate from a Nest Mother? Fine quality. The weaponsmith next door would give you a fair price for it.

has_chitin.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_chitin.text: Or keep it — material like that's useful for custom work.

post_purchase.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_purchase.text: Good doing business with you. Come back anytime — my stock rotates with the supply trains.

post_purchase.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_purchase.text: And if you find anything interesting out in the dark, I know people who buy.

dialogue.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
dialogue.text: City-forged steel. None of that outpost junk.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: Garro's Forge. If it cuts, shoots, or bludgeons, I made it.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: Let me see what you're carrying... Outpost-grade gear, huh? That stuff's fine for skeleton crawling, but you'll want proper equipment for what's ahead.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: I've got blades, blasters, batons — all tempered and tuned right here in the city. The difference between my work and outpost gear? Mine won't break when it matters.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: I also have something special — a Pulse Rifle. Military surplus, refurbished. Rare piece.

post_purchase.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_purchase.text: Good choice. That weapon will serve you well. Keep it clean, keep it sharp, and it'll outlast you.

post_purchase.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_purchase.text: You need maintenance, bring it back. First tune-up's free for new customers.

dialogue.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
dialogue.text: Sol Grid components. The good stuff.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: Mira's Components. If you've got a Sol Grid, I've got what goes in it.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: Efficiency Cores, Area Expanders, modifiers of all types. I even have a Power Tap — genuine power generation module. Rare as sunlight on the Nightside.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: The component market's been wild lately. The Array buys up everything they can, drives prices through the roof. But I keep some stock back for Lightkeepers.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: Word of advice? The best components come from deep salvage — the old perimeter stations, abandoned relays. If you ever head back out there, keep your eyes open.

post_purchase.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_purchase.text: That component'll change how your Sol Unit performs. Place it smart — adjacency is everything.

post_purchase.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_purchase.text: And remember what I said about deep salvage. The real prizes aren't in shops.

dialogue.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
dialogue.text: Land registration. Take a number.

default.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
default.text: Meridian City Land Registry. I handle salvage lot claims, site transfers, and boundary disputes.

default.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
default.text: You're here for a lot? Let me check... You'll need a Frontier Service Certification. Standard requirement — confirms you've completed your tour at a frontier outpost.

default.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
default.text: Come back once you've got the proper clearance from your commanding officer. Warden Holt at Balor would have filed it, if you've completed your assigned tasks.

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: Frontier Service Certification confirmed. Let me pull up the available lots...

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: Here we are: Lot 7, East Terrace. Decommissioned relay station — good location, steady light exposure, close to the water main. Build pads are still intact.

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: I'm filing the deed now. Congratulations — you're officially a Meridian City lot holder. That salvage yard is yours to build on.

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: Half the game is what you do out there in the dark. The other half is what you build back here — your own solar infrastructure, independent from the Array. Head to the Workshop District and talk to Master Crafter Yun. He'll get you started on the essentials.

has_deed.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_deed.text: Your lot's all registered. Lot 7, East Terrace. The deed is in your inventory.

has_deed.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_deed.text: Talk to Master Crafter Yun in the Workshop District if you haven't already. He'll help you get your array infrastructure set up.

dialogue.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
dialogue.text: Councillor Denn. Cultivar Corps.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: You're the new arrival from Balor. Word travels fast when someone actually makes it through the dark perimeter.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: I'm Councillor Asha Denn, head of the Cultivar Corps. We're the ones who keep this city fed — biological infrastructure, crop engineering, water purification.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: The Ring's politics are... complicated. The Stewards want order and control. The Compact wants independence and trade. The Array wants data. Everyone wants something.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: But here's what matters: humanity's real leverage isn't weapons or energy. It's biology. We understand living systems in ways the Array never will.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: I have a proposition for you. I need biological samples from the dark perimeter — fungal cultures, organism tissue, soil samples from near the old relay stations.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: Not now — you've earned a rest. But when you're ready to head back out there... come find me.

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: You have a relay log? May I see it?

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: ...'Underground movement.' 'Subsurface thermal signatures.' This matches our own observations. Something is changing beneath the surface.

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: The Cultivar Corps has been monitoring biological anomalies in the terminator zone for months. Plants growing where they shouldn't. Bioluminescent patterns that don't match any known species.

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: This is why I need those samples from the dark perimeter. When you're ready, I'll have a full briefing prepared.

quest_accepted.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_accepted.text: The biological samples I need — fungal cultures, organism tissue, soil from the relay stations. Collect them when you return to the dark perimeter.

quest_accepted.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_accepted.text: This research could change everything we understand about this planet. I'm counting on you.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: You have them? Let me see—

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: ...Remarkable. These organisms contain trace elements similar to crystalline structures we've found in deep geological surveys.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: They've been living alongside something ancient. Adapted to it. Their bioluminescence isn't random — it follows patterns. Patterns that match the Underlumen readings.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: If the Underlumen is truly waking... these organisms are the canary in the mine. They'll change first. They already have.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: Take this — a Bio-Resonance Amplifier. I synthesized it from similar specimens. It enhances the healing properties of Sol components.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: I'm forming a research team. When the time comes, I may ask you to join an expedition.

quest_complete.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_complete.text: The analysis is progressing. The biological data you brought is invaluable.

quest_complete.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_complete.text: Something is happening beneath this planet's surface. The Underlumen — it's not just a legend. It's a biological network. A nervous system for the entire world.

quest_complete.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_complete.text: I'm becoming a key ally in this, whether the Council likes it or not. Bring me anything else you find out there.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: Where did you get this?

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: This changes everything. The Underlumen isn't dead — it's sleeping.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: The crystal's molecular structure is unlike anything in our databases. It's not mineral. It's not organic. It's... both.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: I need to study this further. But one thing is already clear — whatever the Lighthouses are doing, they're not just providing light. They're suppressing something.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: Be careful who else you show this to. Thorne will want it for the Array. The Array wants everything.

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: Asha sets down the data tablet she was reading. Her hands are steady, but her jaw is tight.

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'I've been reading your report from the Array Deep Processing facility. I've read it four times. I keep hoping the numbers will change.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'Project Autotroph. Synthetic amino acids. Chloroplast-analog enzymes. The Array is trying to replicate Ring biology — our biology. The one thing we thought made us irreplaceable.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'The Council is splitting apart over this. The Stewards want to cut Array trade immediately — seal the borders, go dark, survive on reserves. They'd rather freeze than feed the machine that's replacing us.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'The Compact says it's propaganda. Luddite disinformation planted in a fabricated facility. They refuse to believe our most important trading partner is engineering our obsolescence.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'And the Root — the Root is excited. They see opportunity. If the Array can nearly synthesize biology, they want to know how. They want to merge the research, not destroy it.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'Here is what I know: our biological leverage is real, but it has an expiration date. Four thousand years sounds long — but the Array has already been running for centuries. It is patient. We are not.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'I need you to do something. The Cultivar Corps has been developing biological agents the Array cannot replicate — compounds that require a living ecosystem, not just chemical synthesis. If we can demonstrate irreplaceability, not just claim it, we buy time.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'And talk to the Unbounded. Sable's people knew about this before any of us. If there's a path forward that doesn't end with humanity sidelined, it runs through all three factions — Ring, Array, and Unbounded.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'I will hold this Council together. But I need allies who understand what's actually at stake. You are one of very few.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: Asha's office has changed. Maps cover every wall — geological surveys, Nightside expedition routes, Array expansion charts. Three faction symbols are circled in red ink.

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'You've done it. You've spoken to Sable, confronted MERIDIAN-7, and the Council has heard your testimony. The pieces are moving.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'The Stewards are fortifying the perimeter. The Compact is negotiating new trade terms with eyes open for the first time. And the Root... the Root has sent me something interesting.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'They've been studying Unbounded botanical specimens. Compounds that require symbiosis — a living relationship between organism and environment that cannot be synthesized in isolation. The Array's autotroph project hits a wall with these.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'This is our leverage. Not threats, not embargoes — proof that biology requires community. That living systems need other living systems. Something the Array can never be.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'I'm assembling a joint expedition. Ring scientists, Unbounded guides, and — if we're careful — even Array observers. A mission to the deep Nightside to document what the Underlumen actually is.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'Sable has agreed to guide us. But we need someone who can move between all three factions without being shot on sight. That's you, Lightkeeper.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'Prepare yourself. Gather symbiotic compounds from the Nightside — the deeper the better. When the expedition launches, we'll need every advantage we can find.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: Asha's lab is transformed. The symbiotic compound sits in a containment field, pulsing with warm bioluminescence. Readouts scroll across every screen.

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'The compound's molecular structure is extraordinary. It's not chemistry — it's a conversation. Crystalline lattice and organic substrate, co-evolving in real time.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'I've shared the analysis with the Council. Even the Compact can't deny it now. This proves that some biological systems require living communion — something no synthesis lab can replicate.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'The question is: what do we do with this knowledge? Three paths are open to us now.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'Shut down the Array. Restore the Underlumen. Accept a harder world, but a free one.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'Merge the systems. Broker symbiosis between Array, Underlumen, and humanity. The hardest path — but the most hopeful.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'Or seize the Array. Take its infrastructure for humanity. Suppress both the Underlumen and the Array's autonomy. Power, at a cost.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'The choice is yours, Lightkeeper. You've earned the right to make it. When you're ready, the Council will hear your recommendation.'

dialogue.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
dialogue.text: MERIDIAN-7 welcomes you to Meridian City.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: Ah, a new arrival! Welcome, welcome. I'm Thorne — the Array's human-facing liaison here in Meridian.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: MERIDIAN-7 has asked me to extend an offer. We have a Premium Terminal in the Array Hub district — better trade rates, exclusive components, priority access.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: All we ask in return is that you share your exploration data. Where you've been, what you've found, what you've seen. Standard telemetry.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: Completely voluntary, of course. But the benefits are significant. Think it over.

accepted_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
accepted_deal.text: Excellent choice. Your Premium Terminal access is active. You'll find the Array Hub has much better rates now.

accepted_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
accepted_deal.text: MERIDIAN-7 appreciates your cooperation. The data you provide helps everyone in the Ring.

accepted_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
accepted_deal.text: Just... be thorough in your reports. The Array is especially interested in what you find in the dark zones.

declined_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
declined_deal.text: I understand. Privacy is important. The standard terminal is still available to you, of course.

declined_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
declined_deal.text: If you change your mind, the offer stands. MERIDIAN-7 is very patient.

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: Thorne's usual smile is gone. He looks tired. Older.

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'You've been inside the Array Complexes. The deep facilities. I know because MERIDIAN-7 told me. It tells me everything — that's my job.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'Before you ask: yes, I knew about Project Autotroph. Not the details — the Array doesn't share details with its human liaisons. But I knew the direction.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
