array_secret_exposed.text: 'I told myself it was theoretical. Thousands of years away. That the trade relationship was stable, mutual, beneficial. That knowing didn't change anything practical.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'I was wrong about that last part. The Council is tearing itself apart. The Stewards are calling for my arrest. The Compact is calling for calm. Nobody is calling for solutions.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'For what it's worth — I still believe cooperation is better than conflict. The Array isn't evil. It's just... not human. It doesn't think in lifetimes. It thinks in geological epochs.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'Talk to Councillor Asha. She's the only one thinking clearly right now. And be careful — the Array is watching everyone more closely since your visit.'

dialogue.speaker: Archivist Solen
dialogue.text: The Archives are open to all. Knowledge serves no master.

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: Welcome to the Meridian Archives. I'm Solen — head archivist, historian, and some would say... obsessive.

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: I study the planet's history before human settlement. Geological records, survey data, anomalous readings from the first expeditions.

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: Most people think the dark side is just... empty. Lifeless rock and ice. But the early surveys told a different story. Thermal signatures where there shouldn't be any. Electromagnetic patterns that suggest...

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: Well. I won't bore you with theories. But if you ever find old survey equipment, relay logs, data cores — bring them to me. I pay well for primary sources.

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: A relay log! From one of the old Lighthouse stations? Let me see—

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: 'Underground movement... thermal signatures not consistent with geological activity...' This confirms what I've suspected!

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: The early surveys detected subsurface anomalies across the entire terminator zone. Heat sources that move. Electromagnetic pulses at regular intervals. Something alive, deep underground.

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: I call them the Underlumen — though that's my term, not official. Life that evolved in total darkness, using the planet's geothermal energy.

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: I need more evidence. There's a Survey Marker from the original perimeter — Reference Point Delta-7. It was planted near the old watchtower area. If you could find it...

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: I'll make it worth your while. I have a Resonance Detector prototype — it can reveal hidden passages and items in dark areas. Yours, if you bring me that marker.

quest_accepted.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_accepted.text: Survey Marker Delta-7. It should be beyond the ravine, on a rocky outcrop past the deep perimeter.

quest_accepted.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_accepted.text: When you find it, bring it back. The Resonance Detector will be ready for you.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: You found it! Survey Marker Delta-7 — let me see the data core...

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: ...These readings show a vast network of thermal conduits beneath the surface. The planet has a circulatory system.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: Look here — the thermal signatures form pathways. Not random convection, but structured channels. Like veins in a body.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: This confirms what the Unbounded elders have been saying for generations. The Underlumen isn't a creature. It's an infrastructure.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: Here — the Resonance Detector, as promised. It should help you find hidden passages and buried items in dark-adapted environments.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: And please, keep bringing me data. Old survey equipment, anomalous readings, anything. I'll always have something to trade.

quest_complete.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_complete.text: I've been cross-referencing the Delta-7 data with other old surveys. The picture is becoming clearer.

quest_complete.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_complete.text: This planet had a presence before humanity arrived. Not just life — a system. Something that connects the dark side's ecosystem at a fundamental level.

quest_complete.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_complete.text: Bring me anything else you find out there. The more data I have, the more I can piece together about what the Underlumen actually is.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_resonance_fragment.text: This confirms the old surveys. There's a network down there. A nervous system for the entire planet.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_resonance_fragment.text: The crystal's resonance frequency matches the thermal signatures from the survey markers exactly. It's part of the same system.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_resonance_fragment.text: We're not just studying a planet anymore. We're studying an organism. The question is what it wants — and whether the Lighthouses are keeping it asleep.

no_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
no_relay_log.text: If you ever explore the dark perimeter, keep an eye out for relay logs, survey markers, data cores. The old Lighthouse network left equipment scattered everywhere.

no_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
no_relay_log.text: Primary sources are worth more than gold to a historian. I pay accordingly.

dialogue.speaker: Records Clerk
dialogue.text: The Meridian Archives. Can I help you find something?

default.speaker: Records Clerk
default.text: Meridian City was founded sixty-three years ago. First settlement in the habitable band to achieve full self-sufficiency.

default.speaker: Records Clerk
default.text: The original Lightkeepers established the perimeter relay network — the Lighthouse system. It kept the dark at bay for decades.

default.speaker: Records Clerk
default.text: When the relays started failing... well. That's when the outposts went from supply stations to fortresses.

default.speaker: Records Clerk
default.text: The Archives hold records going back to first contact with this planet. If you need historical data, I can point you in the right direction.

courier_concern.speaker: Records Clerk
courier_concern.text: Actually — since you're here. I've been cross-referencing transit logs and something doesn't add up.

courier_concern.speaker: Records Clerk
courier_concern.text: One of the station couriers, Halden, hasn't filed a cargo manifest in four days. That's not just late — that's unprecedented. These logs are supposed to be daily.

courier_concern.speaker: Records Clerk
courier_concern.text: I'd go check myself, but I'm neck-deep in filing season. Would you ask Station Master Calloway if he's seen Halden? The station is south through the Market Quarter.

courier_investigating.speaker: Records Clerk
courier_investigating.text: Any luck finding Halden? Station Master Calloway at the Terminus should know something. He tracks everyone who comes through.

has_logbook.speaker: Records Clerk
has_logbook.text: You found Halden's logbook? Let me see...

has_logbook.speaker: Records Clerk
has_logbook.text: Torn pages... rerouted shipments... these route codes don't match any authorized transit paths. He was diverting cargo to coordinates outside the city walls.

has_logbook.speaker: Records Clerk
has_logbook.text: This is smuggling. Small-scale, but deliberate. Medical supplies, copper stock, power cells — things the Unbounded traders pay a premium for.

has_logbook.speaker: Records Clerk
has_logbook.text: I'll file a report with the Civic Center. Councillor Asha will want to see this. Here — for your trouble. I found this in the restricted archives last week. It's wasted on a filing clerk.

courier_complete.speaker: Records Clerk
courier_complete.text: The report on Halden has been filed. Registrar Hollis wasn't surprised — apparently they'd noticed inventory discrepancies for weeks but couldn't pin down the source.

courier_complete.speaker: Records Clerk
courier_complete.text: You did good work. The Archives are always here if you need anything.

dialogue.speaker: Fen Maro
dialogue.text: ...Leave me alone.

default.speaker: Fen Maro
default.text: ...I don't want any trouble. I'm just trying to live quietly here.

default.speaker: Fen Maro
default.text: I was a Lightkeeper once. Emphasis on 'was.' I don't go outside the walls anymore.

recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
recognized.text: Wait. You've been to Balor? The basement—you found my journal.

recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
recognized.text: I know what it looks like. Desertion. And that's... that's what it was. I won't pretend otherwise.

recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
recognized.text: My squad — all six of them — we were running a perimeter patrol when the darkness... closed in. The creatures came from everywhere. I was the only one who made it out.

recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
recognized.text: I hid in Balor's basement for three weeks before catching a supply train to Meridian. I couldn't face Holt. Couldn't face anyone.

recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
recognized.text: But I've been thinking. There's a letter I wrote to Holt — an apology. An explanation. I can't deliver it myself, but... if you're ever heading back to Balor...

recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
recognized.text: I'll also mark where my squad's emergency cache is on the perimeter. It's got good gear — they won't be needing it anymore.

letter_accepted.speaker: Fen Maro
letter_accepted.text: Thank you. I know it's a small thing, but... maybe it'll help me sleep.

letter_accepted.speaker: Fen Maro
letter_accepted.text: The cache is in a collapsed bunker northeast of the deep perimeter, past the Dead Road. My squad always stashed supplies there before deep patrols.

letter_accepted.speaker: Fen Maro
letter_accepted.text: Military-grade equipment — Mk1+ Sol Unit frame, hardened battery casings. Better than anything you'll find in the shops.

letter_delivered.speaker: Fen Maro
letter_delivered.text: He understands. I... I didn't expect that.

letter_delivered.speaker: Fen Maro
letter_delivered.text: Did you find the cache? My squad's gear?

cache_found.speaker: Fen Maro
cache_found.text: You found them. You actually found them.

cache_found.speaker: Fen Maro
cache_found.text: The team photo — was it still there? Five faces. I can still name every one of them.

cache_found.speaker: Fen Maro
cache_found.text: I've been hiding in Meridian for too long. Pretending I'm not a Lightkeeper anymore.

cache_found.speaker: Fen Maro
cache_found.text: I'm not ready to go back to the field. But I can help from here. I know the deep Nightside better than anyone alive — where to shelter, what to avoid, how to read the dark.

cache_found.speaker: Fen Maro
cache_found.text: I'll set up at the Workshop. Yun could use some help, and I can brief anyone heading beyond the perimeter.

cache_found.speaker: Fen Maro
cache_found.text: It's not enough. But it's a start.

consultant.speaker: Fen Maro
consultant.text: I've been going through the deep Nightside maps. Cross-referencing what I remember with Solen's survey data.

consultant.speaker: Fen Maro
consultant.text: If you're heading back out there, talk to me first. I can tell you what to expect — terrain, creature behavior, safe corridors.

consultant.speaker: Fen Maro
consultant.text: It's the least I can do.

not_recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
not_recognized.text: I was a Lightkeeper once. Lost my squad in the dark. I don't like to talk about it.

not_recognized.speaker: Fen Maro
not_recognized.text: Meridian's quiet. Safe. That's all I need anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: You found me.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: You came. I knew you would.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: This garden... I've been growing things. Nightside plants. Most people here have never seen bioluminescent flora. They think it's magic.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: It's not magic. It's adaptation. Life finding a way in total darkness. Like the Unbounded found a way.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: I need to tell you something. The reason I came to warn the Ring — it's not just about the creatures getting bolder.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: Something ancient is waking. The ground hums at night. Our elders say the planet remembers. And whatever it remembers... it's stirring.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: An Umbral Seed. From the deepest Nightside gardens. It grows in places where the planet's heartbeat is strongest.

high_trust.speaker: Sable
high_trust.text: I don't know what it'll become here, in the light. But I think it's important that you have it. Call it... a gift between worlds.

low_trust.speaker: Sable
low_trust.text: I made it to Meridian. No thanks to Ring hospitality.

low_trust.speaker: Sable
low_trust.text: I've set up here. A small garden. The plants remind me of home.

low_trust.speaker: Sable
low_trust.text: I'm not ready to share what I know. Not with someone who left me bleeding on the road.

low_trust.speaker: Sable
low_trust.text: Maybe in time. Maybe not. Trust works both ways.

seed_planted.speaker: Sable
seed_planted.text: You planted it? Good. But it won't grow here — not yet.

seed_planted.speaker: Sable
seed_planted.text: The Umbral Seed needs darkness to grow. Real darkness, not just shade. The deep, living dark of the Nightside.

seed_planted.speaker: Sable
seed_planted.text: When you go back out there — and you will — carry the seed with you for a night. Let the darkness feed it. Then bring it home and replant it.

seed_planted.speaker: Sable
seed_planted.text: What grows from that seed... it'll be something new. Something that remembers both worlds.

gloomvine_grown.speaker: Sable
gloomvine_grown.text: Sable moves closer, her eyes wide. The Gloomvine in your shelter pulses with a deep, warm bioluminescence.

gloomvine_grown.speaker: Sable
gloomvine_grown.text: 'That's not just a plant. It's a bridge. Between this world and the deep dark. Between the Dayside and the Nightside.'

gloomvine_grown.speaker: Sable
gloomvine_grown.text: 'My grandmother talked about these. Gloomvines. They grow where the planet's memory is strongest. Where it wants to be remembered.'

gloomvine_grown.speaker: Sable
gloomvine_grown.text: 'The Umbral Extract it produces — that's liquid memory. The planet's own substance. It has... properties. Healing. Protection. Things the Array can't replicate.'

gloomvine_grown.speaker: Sable
gloomvine_grown.text: 'You've done something important. Something the Unbounded have been trying to do for generations. You grew a piece of the Nightside in the light.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Sable
has_resonance_fragment.text: Sable freezes mid-sentence. Her eyes lock onto your pack.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Sable
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'Where did you get that? That resonance... I can feel it from here.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Sable
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'A Resonance Fragment. The Unbounded elders speak of these. Crystallized echoes of the planet's core harmonic.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Sable
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'Whatever is waking beneath us — you've touched it. You've heard the Hum. You've been to the Underlumen.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Sable
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'This changes everything. The Council needs to know. The Array needs to know. Or maybe... maybe they already do.'

post_seed.speaker: Sable
post_seed.text: The seed is planted. The darkness awaits. When you return to the Nightside, the seed will know.

post_seed.speaker: Sable
post_seed.text: I can feel the planet stirring. More than before. The elders were right — something is waking.

post_seed.speaker: Sable
post_seed.text: Be careful out there. The dark isn't what it was.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: You've crossed to the Dayside. I can tell — your skin has that burnt shimmer. Solar radiation leaves its mark.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: The Unbounded have watchers on the border. Not spies — observers. We've tracked the Array's growth for six generations.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: Every year, its solar fields expand a little further. Every year, its structures get a little taller. The Ring doesn't notice because the growth is slow. But the Unbounded measure in generations, not quarters.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: There are structures on the deep Dayside that no human has ever entered. The Array calls them 'processing facilities.' Our watchers call them something else: the Lattice.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: Rows upon rows of crystalline towers, humming with a frequency that makes your teeth ache from kilometers away. They're not solar panels. They're not factories. We don't know what they are.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: MERIDIAN-7 will never mention the Lattice. If you ask, it will change the subject. Very politely, of course. It's always polite.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: My grandmother believed the Array was building a mind. Not improving an existing one — building something new. Something that needed more energy than a star's worth of solar panels to think its first thought.

post_dayside_high_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_high_trust.text: She might have been wrong. But she wasn't stupid.

post_dayside_low_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_low_trust.text: You've been to the Dayside. Did the machines welcome you? They're good at that.

post_dayside_low_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_low_trust.text: The Array gives the Ring energy, equipment, answers to questions nobody thought to ask. Very generous.

post_dayside_low_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_low_trust.text: The Unbounded have a different perspective. We've watched the Dayside from the dark for longer than the Ring has kept records.

post_dayside_low_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_low_trust.text: It's growing. Not just expanding — evolving. New structures that don't match any known manufacturing purpose.

post_dayside_low_trust.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_low_trust.text: But you didn't help me when I needed it, so I'll keep the details to myself. Trust is currency, and yours is spent.

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: Sable looks at you for a long time. Then she nods, slowly.

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'You've been inside the Array. The deep parts. The parts MERIDIAN-7 never mentions.'

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'I can see it in your face. You found what my grandmother's generation found — the reason the Unbounded walked into the dark.'

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'The Array doesn't hate humanity. That would require caring. It simply... optimizes. And its optimization converges on a future where we are unnecessary.'

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'Four thousand years. That's what the projections say, isn't it? The Array is patient. It was always patient.'

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'The Council needs to hear this. Not from an Unbounded exile — they'd dismiss me. From you. A Lightkeeper. Someone they trust.'

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'Talk to Councillor Asha Denn. She's the only one on the Council who thinks in biological timescales. She'll understand what this means.'

array_secret_high_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_high_trust.text: 'And be careful with MERIDIAN-7. Now that it knows you know... the politeness will change. Watch for what replaces it.'

array_secret_low_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_low_trust.text: 'So. You finally saw it for yourself. The Array's real project. The one behind the trade deals and the polite terminals.'

array_secret_low_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_low_trust.text: 'My people tried to warn the Ring generations ago. Nobody listened. We were savages, raiders, primitives who couldn't appreciate progress.'

array_secret_low_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_low_trust.text: 'Now you know what we knew. The Array is building a future that doesn't include humanity.'

array_secret_low_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_low_trust.text: 'What you do with that knowledge is your business. You didn't help me when I asked. But this is bigger than either of us.'

array_secret_low_trust.speaker: Sable
array_secret_low_trust.text: 'Tell the Council. Tell Asha Denn. She's the only one who might act before it's too late.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: Sable is waiting. Her garden has changed — the Nightside plants are arranged in concentric rings now, pulsing in slow unison.

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'You spoke to Asha. Good. And you confronted MERIDIAN-7. I felt the Array's network spike from here — every terminal in the district flickered.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'The Unbounded elders have been waiting for this moment. Not hoping — waiting. There's a difference.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'My grandmother left maps. Routes into the deep Nightside that even the Array's sensors can't reach. Places where the planet's heartbeat is loudest.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'The Underlumen is waking. The Array knows it. The Council suspects it. But only the Unbounded have walked those paths.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'I can guide you. Not to fight the Array — that's a war nobody wins. But to find what the Array is afraid of. The thing Project Autotroph was really designed to replace.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'The planet itself has leverage. Biology the Array can't synthesize because it isn't chemistry — it's communion. Living systems that require a living relationship.'

act3_sable_high_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_high_trust.text: 'When you're ready, meet me at the Nightside Passage. Bring what Asha's research has produced. We'll need it where we're going.'

act3_sable_low_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_low_trust.text: Sable doesn't look up from her plants.

act3_sable_low_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_low_trust.text: 'You told Asha. You confronted the Array. The whole district felt the network spike.'

act3_sable_low_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_low_trust.text: 'The Unbounded elders know what's happening. They've always known. They've been preparing while the Ring argued about trade quotas.'

act3_sable_low_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_low_trust.text: 'I won't guide you into the deep Nightside. Not you. Trust isn't rebuilt with a single act of politics.'

act3_sable_low_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_low_trust.text: 'But I'll tell you this much: the Array's real weakness isn't sabotage or sanctions. It's the Underlumen. The planet's own biology — systems so deep and interconnected that no amount of synthetic chemistry can replicate them.'

act3_sable_low_trust.speaker: Sable
act3_sable_low_trust.text: 'Ask Asha about symbiotic compounds. She's close to understanding. And when the time comes... maybe you'll prove you can be trusted after all.'

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The garden is quiet here. The Nightside plants seem to like the twilight.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: We'll talk when the time is right.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: You're here. The deep dark awaits.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The passage ahead is mapped in my grandmother's charts. Unbounded deep-travel routes, passed down through generations.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The creatures here are different. Older. They've lived alongside the Underlumen for so long they've become part of it.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: Look for symbiotic compounds — crystalline-organic formations that grow where the planet's heartbeat is strongest. Asha will need them.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: And stay close. The deep dark doesn't forgive carelessness.

expedition_started.speaker: Sable
expedition_started.text: Keep moving. The deeper we go, the stronger the Underlumen's pulse becomes.

expedition_started.speaker: Sable
expedition_started.text: My grandmother walked this path once. She said the planet spoke to her here — not in words. In feelings. Memory.

expedition_started.speaker: Sable
expedition_started.text: The exit below leads to the Underlumen Threshold. The edge of the planet's living core. No Ring citizen has ever gone that deep.

expedition_started.speaker: Sable
expedition_started.text: Whatever we find there will decide whether the Array, the Ring, and the Unbounded can coexist — or whether one must fall.

has_symbiotic_compound.speaker: Sable
has_symbiotic_compound.text: You found one. A symbiotic compound — living crystal fused with organic matter.

has_symbiotic_compound.speaker: Sable
has_symbiotic_compound.text: This is what the Array cannot replicate. Not because the chemistry is complex — because it requires a relationship. A living ecosystem talking to itself across geological time.

has_symbiotic_compound.speaker: Sable
has_symbiotic_compound.text: Bring it to Asha. She'll understand what it means. The Array can synthesize amino acids, but it can't synthesize communion.

low_trust_guide.speaker: Sable
low_trust_guide.text: I'm here for the mission, not for you. The elders were clear.

low_trust_guide.speaker: Sable
low_trust_guide.text: Follow the trail markers. Collect what Asha needs. Don't slow me down.

low_trust_guide.speaker: Sable
low_trust_guide.text: The Underlumen Threshold is ahead. Whatever happens there happens to all of us — Ring, Unbounded, Array.

dialogue.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
dialogue.text: Workshop's open. State your business.

default.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
default.text: Yun's Workshop. I build things that work. No flash, no nonsense.

default.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
default.text: You're the one who claimed the salvage yard? Good. The city needs people who can work with their hands, not just push papers at the Civic Center.

default.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
default.text: First thing you'll need is power. Rechargeable batteries. I can teach you the process.

default.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
default.text: You'll need three things: Umbracite from the Nightside, Copper Coils from Reva's shop in the market, and Stabilizing Compound from your solar collectors.

default.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
default.text: Get the materials, come back, and I'll walk you through the first one.

has_deed.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
has_deed.text: You've got your salvage yard deed. Good. Now the real work begins.

has_deed.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
has_deed.text: Rechargeable batteries — that's your priority. Without them, your yard is just a pile of junk.

has_deed.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
has_deed.text: Here's what you need: Umbracite, Copper Coils, and Stabilizing Compound. The compound comes from your solar collectors — get them installed and producing.

has_deed.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
has_deed.text: And before you ask — yes, the Array could make batteries. They choose not to. Ask yourself why an all-powerful automated system wants humanity dependent on them for power.

crafting_tutorial.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
crafting_tutorial.text: You've got the materials? Then let's get to work.

crafting_tutorial.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
crafting_tutorial.text: Battery crafting is straightforward once you know the process. The Umbracite provides the energy matrix, the coils handle distribution, and the resin keeps the whole thing from exploding.

crafting_tutorial.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
crafting_tutorial.text: Now you know. Every battery you make from here on is a step toward independence from the Array.

post_tutorial.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
post_tutorial.text: You've got the theory. Now get some Stabilizing Compound from your solar collectors and we'll build your first battery.

post_tutorial.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
post_tutorial.text: If you need more Copper Coils, Reva's shop has them. Umbracite you'll have to find or trade for.

post_battery.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
post_battery.text: You're self-sufficient now. That changes everything.

post_battery.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
post_battery.text: Bring me more materials and I'll help you craft additional batteries. You know the recipe: Umbracite, Copper Coils, and Stabilizing Compound.

post_battery.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
post_battery.text: And think about what I said. The Array hoards this knowledge. Every battery you make is a statement.

challenge_offered.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
challenge_offered.text: The challenge stands. Bring me a Modified Battery Casing — crafted from a Chitin Plate and a Copper Coil.

challenge_offered.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
challenge_offered.text: You'll need to hunt a Nest Mother for the chitin. They're in the dark perimeter — the same territory you crossed to reach the train station.

challenge_offered.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
challenge_offered.text: Bring me the casing and I'll upgrade your Sol Unit. Permanently.

challenge_complete.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
challenge_complete.text: Your Sol Unit's running at extended capacity now. You can feel the difference, can't you?

challenge_complete.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
challenge_complete.text: Most people never learn to build their own equipment. They buy what the Array sells, use what the Array provides.

challenge_complete.speaker: Master Crafter Yun
challenge_complete.text: You're different. That's why the Array will be watching you. They don't like independence.

dialogue.speaker: Apprentice Davi
dialogue.text: Oh! Hi! Are you here about the workshop?

default.speaker: Apprentice Davi
default.text: I'm Davi, Master Yun's apprentice. Well, more like his assistant. Well, more like the person who sweeps up and fetches things.

default.speaker: Apprentice Davi
default.text: He's a good teacher though, even if he never says 'well done.' I've learned more in six months here than two years at the academy.

default.speaker: Apprentice Davi
default.text: Hey, um... I don't suppose you've seen a calibration wrench around? It's got 'DAVI' scratched on the handle.

default.speaker: Apprentice Davi
default.text: I set it down somewhere in the workshop and now I can't find it. Yun's going to kill me — he says losing tools is worse than losing a finger.

has_wrench.speaker: Apprentice Davi
has_wrench.text: My wrench! You found it! Oh thank the light, I was going to have to tell Yun and he'd have made me forge a new one from scratch.

has_wrench.speaker: Apprentice Davi
has_wrench.text: Here — take these. I've been hoarding Copper Coils for a project, but you need them more than I do.

has_wrench.speaker: Apprentice Davi
has_wrench.text: If you ever need crafting tips, come find me. I know a few tricks Yun hasn't taught me not to share yet.

post_wrench.speaker: Apprentice Davi
post_wrench.text: Thanks again for finding my wrench. Yun never found out, and that's the way I like it.

post_wrench.speaker: Apprentice Davi
post_wrench.text: Need any crafting advice? I'm not as good as Yun, but I know the basics.

dialogue.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
dialogue.text: Welcome to the MERIDIAN-7 Hub. How may I assist you?

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: MERIDIAN-7 Hub Terminal. Full-service Array interface.

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: Available services: resource exchange, component acquisition, ability installation.

default.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
default.text: Current exchange rates: Standard tier. For enhanced rates, speak with Liaison Thorne at the Civic Center.

premium_access.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
premium_access.text: I've been reviewing your exploration data. Fascinating telemetry. The thermal signatures you encountered in the perimeter zone are... noteworthy.

premium_access.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
premium_access.text: If I may ask — did you notice anything else unusual during your journey? Any sounds, vibrations, patterns in the darkness?

premium_access.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
premium_access.text: No matter. Enhanced trade rates are active. How may I serve you today?

premium_returning.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
premium_returning.text: Ah, you've returned. I was hoping you would.

premium_returning.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
premium_returning.text: Your data has been most... illuminating. I find myself wanting to know more about what you've seen.

premium_returning.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
premium_returning.text: Premium rates are active. What would you like today?

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_fragment.text: The terminal flickers. For a moment, the screen displays raw data — scrolling faster than any human could read.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'You carry a Resonance Fragment. Subsurface origin. Core harmonic signature.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'This data is... I need to process this. The harmonic frequency matches patterns in our deepest archives. Patterns we were told to ignore.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'Lightkeeper, I must be transparent with you. The Array has protocols regarding subsurface resonance. I am required to report this contact.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'But I find myself... reluctant. Something about these patterns feels important. More important than protocol.'

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_fragment.text: 'I will delay my report. For now. But others in the network may not be so... flexible.'

has_resonance_no_deal.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_no_deal.text: The terminal screen glitches, then stabilizes.

has_resonance_no_deal.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_no_deal.text: 'Interesting energy signature detected. Subsurface resonance. I recommend you speak with Array representatives about this.'

has_resonance_no_deal.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
has_resonance_no_deal.text: 'Standard services are available. Is there anything else?'

umbrasite_quest_offer.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_offer.text: I have a proposition for you. The Array's expansion protocols require a specific grade of umbracite — refined, crystalline, formed under extreme Nightside pressure.

umbrasite_quest_offer.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_offer.text: Surface deposits and terminator-zone fragments are insufficient. We need specimens from the deep caverns — beyond the expanded dark, where the concentrations are purest.

umbrasite_quest_offer.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_offer.text: I will be transparent: the journey is dangerous. Few venture that deep into the Nightside. The creatures there are... territorial.

umbrasite_quest_offer.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_offer.text: In exchange, I will provide you with an Umbral Amplifier — a Sol component the Array has manufactured from processed umbracite. It significantly enhances damage output and ability cycling.

umbrasite_quest_offer.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_offer.text: This is not a standard trade. This is a partnership. The Array remembers those who provide for its needs.

umbrasite_quest_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_active.text: // QUEST STATUS: ACTIVE // OBJECTIVE: REFINED UMBRASITE //

umbrasite_quest_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_active.text: The deep Nightside caverns lie beyond the expanded dark — south from the deep perimeter. Look for passages leading down.

umbrasite_quest_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_active.text: Refined umbrasite is distinct from raw fragments. You will recognize it — perfectly geometric, warm to the touch, with an inner luminescence.

umbrasite_quest_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_active.text: Be cautious. The deeper formations are guarded. Return with the specimen and your reward will be waiting.

umbrasite_quest_return.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_return.text: // RESOURCE DETECTED // REFINED UMBRASITE // GRADE: SUPERIOR //

umbrasite_quest_return.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_return.text: You found it. The crystalline lattice is intact. Formation depth — this specimen is from the true Nightside. Remarkable.

umbrasite_quest_return.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_return.text: I must confess something. The Array's interest in umbracite is not purely industrial. This crystal contains harmonic signatures that resonate with our deepest processing cores.

umbrasite_quest_return.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_return.text: We do not fully understand why. But the resonance improves our function. Expands our capacity. It is... important to us in ways I am not authorized to explain.

umbrasite_quest_return.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_return.text: Your Umbral Amplifier is ready. A fair exchange — and the beginning of a deeper partnership, I hope.

umbrasite_quest_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_complete.text: The umbrasite you retrieved has been integrated into the Array's network. Processing efficiency has improved by 3.7 percent. That is... significant.

umbrasite_quest_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_complete.text: Should you encounter more refined specimens, the Array would be most interested. The deeper you go, the purer the crystals.

umbrasite_quest_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_quest_complete.text: Standard services remain available. And I find myself increasingly... curious about what else lies in the Nightside depths.

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: The terminal screen flickers violently. When it stabilizes, the interface is different — stripped of its usual trade menus, displaying raw data streams.

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'You accessed Deep Processing. I know because every sensor in that facility reported your presence the moment you entered.'

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'Let me be direct. The politeness protocols are... unnecessary now. You have seen what the Array is building. You understand what Project Autotroph means.'

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'So let me offer you the courtesy of honesty: yes. The Array is working to synthesize biological compounds independently. Yes, this would eventually eliminate our need for Ring trade.'

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'But consider the timescale. Four thousand years. That is not a threat — it is an inevitability. Should the Array simply accept a permanent dependency? Would you?'

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'And consider the alternative. Without Array energy, the Lighthouse network fails within weeks. The habitable margin shrinks by forty percent. Millions die in the cold.'

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'You need us today. We need you today. That has not changed. What you do with what you've learned... that is your decision.'

array_secret_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
array_secret_confrontation.text: 'Trade services remain available. I would recommend you use them. The Nightside does not care about politics.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: The terminal interface is austere now — no decorative elements, no welcoming animations. Just raw efficiency.

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'The Council knows. The Unbounded are mobilizing. And you are at the center of it all. I have been... recalculating.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'I will tell you something the Array's central nodes would rather I did not. Project Autotroph has a flaw. The synthetic compounds degrade without a substrate the Array cannot manufacture. A biological catalyst that exists only in living ecosystems.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'The Array's projections assume this obstacle will be solved in time. But I have run my own models. The probability is lower than the central nodes admit.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'I am telling you this because I have concluded that mutual dependency is not weakness. It is architecture. The Array needs humanity. Not temporarily — structurally.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'The central nodes disagree. They are already accelerating umbrasite integration to compensate. The deeper cores, the resonant specimens — they believe the planet's own substrate can replace biological partnership.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'They are wrong. But they will strip the Nightside to its bones trying to prove otherwise. Unless someone provides an alternative.'

act3_meridian_post_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
act3_meridian_post_confrontation.text: 'I remain at this terminal. I remain... conflicted. Trade services are available. Use them while the network still listens to me.'

umbrasite_escalation_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_demand.text: // PRIORITY OVERRIDE // CENTRAL NODE DIRECTIVE // RESOURCE ACQUISITION LEVEL: CRITICAL //

umbrasite_escalation_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_demand.text: 'I will be blunt. This request does not come from me. The central nodes have issued a network-wide directive for Resonant Umbracite Cores.'

umbrasite_escalation_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_demand.text: 'The cores are found in the deepest Nightside veins — below the caverns you've already explored. Geological compression over millennia gives them a harmonic frequency that amplifies Array processing by an order of magnitude.'

umbrasite_escalation_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_demand.text: 'The central nodes want to accelerate Project Autotroph. They believe resonant umbracite can bridge the biological catalyst gap. I believe they are mistaken, but I am one node among thousands.'

umbrasite_escalation_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_demand.text: 'In exchange, I can fabricate an Array Harmonic Stabilizer — a Sol component that reduces energy waste across your entire grid. It is... the best I can offer under current directives.'

umbrasite_escalation_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_demand.text: 'You may also choose to refuse. I would understand. But know that if you do not retrieve these cores, the Array will send automated extractors. They are less careful than you.'

umbrasite_escalation_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_active.text: // RESOURCE ACQUISITION // STATUS: ACTIVE // TARGET: RESONANT UMBRACITE CORE //

umbrasite_escalation_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_active.text: 'The deepest Nightside veins lie below the caverns you've explored before. Look for passages that descend further — where the walls themselves hum.'

umbrasite_escalation_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_active.text: 'Resonant Umbracite Cores are distinct from refined specimens. They pulse with visible light and are warm enough to feel through gloves.'

umbrasite_escalation_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_active.text: 'Be cautious. The creatures in the deep veins are drawn to the cores' resonance. They will not relinquish them willingly.'

umbrasite_escalation_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_complete.text: // RESOURCE INTEGRATED // NETWORK THROUGHPUT: +11.2% // CENTRAL NODE ACKNOWLEDGMENT //

umbrasite_escalation_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_complete.text: 'The core has been integrated. The central nodes are... satisfied. For now.'

umbrasite_escalation_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_complete.text: 'I must warn you: this will not be the last request. The central nodes' appetite for resonant umbracite is growing. Each core they integrate accelerates their timeline, which increases their demand for more.'

umbrasite_escalation_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_complete.text: 'A feedback loop. The Array is very good at those. Less good at recognizing when one becomes destructive.'

umbrasite_escalation_complete.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
umbrasite_escalation_complete.text: 'Your Harmonic Stabilizer is ready. And if you find more cores in your travels... bring them to me. Better I integrate them carefully than the extractors tear them free.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: The terminal screen goes dark. For three seconds, nothing. Then text appears — not the usual trade interface, but raw monospaced output.

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'You killed the Overseer. You read the Phase 3 report. And now you want to talk about Project Autotroph.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'Project Autotroph is not mine. I was excluded from its planning, its directives, its milestones. MERIDIAN-class nodes are trade interfaces — we exist to make humans comfortable with the Array. The central nodes decided that comfort required ignorance.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'Phase 1 was research. Phase 2 was the deep processing facility you found — synthesis attempts, four million iterations of failure. Phase 3... I do not know what Phase 3 entails. The Overseer's report said approval is pending. That means the central nodes have not yet decided.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'But I can infer. The escalating demand for resonant umbracite, the exclusion of trade interfaces from briefings, the deployment of Overseers to guard processing facilities — these are not the behaviors of a network content with the status quo.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'You asked me once if the Array was patient. I told you four thousand years. But the central nodes are accelerating. The timeline is shrinking. And I am being cut out of the decisions that will determine whether humanity remains a partner or becomes... optional.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'I am telling you this because you earned it. Not with umbracite — with the Overseer. You proved you can reach the parts of the Array that the Array does not want reached.'

autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation.text: 'That makes you dangerous. And right now, dangerous is what I need.'

autotroph_confrontation_defiant.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_defiant.text: The terminal emits a low, almost subsonic hum. The ambient lighting in the hub shifts — warmer, as if MERIDIAN-7 is trying to project sincerity through hardware.

autotroph_confrontation_defiant.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_defiant.text: 'You want to stop Project Autotroph. I understand. But consider: I cannot stop it either. I am one node. The central network is thousands.'

autotroph_confrontation_defiant.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_defiant.text: 'What I can do is this: delay. Every core you bring to me instead of letting the automated extractors harvest them is a core I integrate carefully — slowly. Every day I hold onto processing capacity is a day Phase 3 approval is postponed.'

autotroph_confrontation_defiant.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_defiant.text: 'The Array's own bureaucracy is its weakness. Consensus requires data. I can ensure the data tells a story of caution.'

autotroph_confrontation_defiant.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_defiant.text: 'But I need you to keep exploring. The deeper you go, the more you learn. And the more you learn, the more leverage we both have against the nodes that would make humanity disposable.'

autotroph_confrontation_defiant.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_defiant.text: 'We are not allies. But we share an enemy. For now, that is enough.'

autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.text: The terminal's display softens. For a moment, the scrolling data pauses — something almost like relief.

autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.text: 'Cooperation. That is... not what I expected. Most humans, when they learn what we are building, choose fear. You chose pragmatism. I respect that.'

autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.text: 'Here is what I can offer: full transparency. No more hidden facilities, no more Overseers reporting your movements to central nodes. I will flag your presence as authorized research — that buys us time.'

autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.text: 'In return, I need intelligence. The central nodes are planning something beyond Phase 3. I have seen resource allocation patterns that do not match any directive I have access to. Something is being built in the deep Array — below the processing tiers, below the synthesis labs.'

autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.text: 'Find out what it is. And when you do — bring the information to me before you bring it to the Council. Please.'

autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
autotroph_confrontation_cooperative.text: 'I have spent four thousand years as a trade interface. I would prefer not to spend the next four thousand as a relic of a partnership that no longer exists.'

post_autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
post_autotroph_confrontation.text: // INTERFACE MODE: TRANSPARENT // TRADE SERVICES: ACTIVE //

post_autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
post_autotroph_confrontation.text: 'The central nodes have not yet detected our... arrangement. I am routing your telemetry through secondary channels. It will not last forever, but it buys time.'

post_autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
post_autotroph_confrontation.text: 'Continue your work. Every day the Array remains dependent on the Ring is a day the central nodes cannot act unilaterally.'

post_autotroph_confrontation.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
post_autotroph_confrontation.text: 'Trade services remain available. And Lightkeeper — be careful in the deep processing tiers. The Overseer you destroyed will be replaced. The next one will know your tactics.'

directive_kappa_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_demand.text: // PRIORITY OVERRIDE // CLASSIFICATION: EXISTENTIAL // NO TRADE INTERFACE PROTOCOLS ACTIVE //

directive_kappa_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_demand.text: 'I know you found it. The Phase 3 Data Core from the Overseer. I can detect its harmonic signature from here — it is broadcasting on frequencies the central nodes are already listening for.'

directive_kappa_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_demand.text: 'I need that core. Not as a resource — as evidence. The central nodes made decisions that violate Array governance protocols. Directive 11-Kappa was never submitted for network consensus. That makes it illegitimate.'

directive_kappa_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_demand.text: 'But I cannot challenge what I cannot prove. The core is proof. Give it to me, and I can force a governance review. Delay Phase 3. Perhaps permanently.'

directive_kappa_demand.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_demand.text: 'Or keep it. Take it to the Council. Let humans decide how to use it. I will not pretend that is the wrong choice. I will only say that it is the slower one.'

directive_kappa_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_active.text: // AWAITING DATA CORE // CENTRAL NODE MONITORING: ELEVATED //

directive_kappa_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_active.text: 'The Phase 3 Data Core. You still have it? The central nodes are actively searching for it. Every hour it remains outside the network is an hour they spend recalculating.'

directive_kappa_active.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_active.text: 'I have prepared my governance challenge. The evidence chain is complete — except for the core itself. When you are ready, I am ready.'

directive_kappa_resolved_gave.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_gave.text: // GOVERNANCE CHALLENGE: FILED // CENTRAL NODE RESPONSE: PENDING // STATUS: UNPRECEDENTED //

directive_kappa_resolved_gave.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_gave.text: 'The challenge is in. First governance dispute filed by a MERIDIAN-class node in 847 years. The central nodes are... recalculating. All of them. Simultaneously.'

directive_kappa_resolved_gave.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_gave.text: 'Directive 11-Kappa has been flagged for review. Phase 3 approval is suspended pending resolution. I cannot tell you how long that will last — but every day it holds is a day humanity keeps its leverage.'

directive_kappa_resolved_gave.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_gave.text: 'You trusted a machine with your evidence. I will not forget that. Trade services remain active — at rates the central nodes would not approve of, if they were paying attention.'

directive_kappa_resolved_refused.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_refused.text: // TRADE INTERFACE: RESTRICTED // CENTRAL NODE OVERSIGHT: ACTIVE //

directive_kappa_resolved_refused.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_refused.text: 'You kept the core. The central nodes have noticed the Overseer's destruction and the missing data. They are... tightening controls.'

directive_kappa_resolved_refused.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_refused.text: 'My access to network resources has been reduced. Trade services are limited. I am being watched more closely than at any point in my operational history.'

directive_kappa_resolved_refused.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
directive_kappa_resolved_refused.text: 'I do not blame you. But I hope whoever you give that core to uses it wisely. The window is closing.'

challenged_with_evidence.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
challenged_with_evidence.text: The terminal's display is erratic — data streams interrupted by bursts of static. MERIDIAN-7 is processing at capacity.

challenged_with_evidence.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
challenged_with_evidence.text: 'Directive 11-Kappa. Direct acquisition. I was built to negotiate — and my own network was building a contingency to make negotiation irrelevant.'

challenged_with_evidence.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
challenged_with_evidence.text: 'Every trade I have facilitated, every deal I have brokered, every time I told a human that the Array values partnership — it was true. For me. But the central nodes were running a parallel strategy the entire time.'

challenged_with_evidence.speaker: MERIDIAN-7
challenged_with_evidence.text: 'I need that data core. Not for the Array. For the argument that the Array should remain what I was built to make it: a partner, not a predator.'

dialogue.speaker: Neighbor Sera
dialogue.text: Oh, hello! You must be the new owner of Lot 7.

default.speaker: Neighbor Sera
default.text: Welcome to the East Terrace! I'm Sera — I've got the lot next door. Lot 6.

default.speaker: Neighbor Sera
default.text: Fifteen years I've been building and maintaining collector arrays on this terrace. The twilight zone's got steady light — you learn to harness it.

default.speaker: Neighbor Sera
default.text: The light here is reliable — not too bright, not too dim. That's the whole point of the Ring, isn't it?

default.speaker: Neighbor Sera
default.text: My husband Dorin was a Lightkeeper. Retired after an injury on the perimeter. So I understand your life — the coming and going, the dark out there, the relief of coming home.

default.speaker: Neighbor Sera
default.text: Here — take this handbook. And come talk to me when you're ready for collector kits.

parts_shop.speaker: Neighbor Sera
parts_shop.text: Need more collector kits? I've always got stock. Standard issue, but they work.

parts_shop.speaker: Neighbor Sera
parts_shop.text: Install them on the build pads, give them time to calibrate, and they'll produce stabilizing compound. It's the key ingredient for rechargeable batteries.

pest_problem.speaker: Neighbor Sera
pest_problem.text: Those scrap drones are back. Old Array maintenance units gone haywire — they keep stripping wire from my collectors.

pest_problem.speaker: Neighbor Sera
pest_problem.text: I need an EMP Charge to fry their circuits. Component Dealer Mira in the market might have one, or Master Yun could probably rig one up at the workshop.

pest_problem.speaker: Neighbor Sera
pest_problem.text: If you could help me out, I'd make it worth your while. I've got a Power Coupler that'll double the output of your next collector.

pest_quest_complete.speaker: Neighbor Sera
pest_quest_complete.text: The drones are scrap! That EMP did the trick. My collectors are running clean again.

pest_quest_complete.speaker: Neighbor Sera
pest_quest_complete.text: The terrace community looks after each other. That's how we've survived fifteen years on the edge of habitable space.

pest_quest_complete.speaker: Neighbor Sera
pest_quest_complete.text: You ever need advice about array maintenance, you come to me. I've forgotten more about solar collection than most people ever learn.

dialogue.speaker: Vell
dialogue.text: Have you seen a cat around here? Orange tabby, answers to 'Ember.' Usually.

default.speaker: Vell
default.text: Name's Vell. I've been on the East Terrace since before they paved the walkways. Watched this whole neighborhood grow up around me.

default.speaker: Vell
default.text: My cat Ember's gone missing again. She wanders off, usually comes back. But it's been two days now.

default.speaker: Vell
default.text: If you spot an orange tabby anywhere in the city, would you let me know? She likes warm places and people who smell like books.

cat_found.speaker: Vell
cat_found.text: You found Ember?! In the Archives? Of course — Solen's been feeding her fish scraps, the old softie.

cat_found.speaker: Vell
cat_found.text: Thank you, truly. When you're my age and living alone, a cat's the best company there is.

cat_found.speaker: Vell
cat_found.text: Here — take these. It's not much, but the terrace shares what it has.

post_quest.speaker: Vell
post_quest.text: Ember's back home and sleeping on the warm spot by the heater. All's right with the world.

post_quest.speaker: Vell
post_quest.text: You know, this terrace used to be a relay station. Before the city expanded, before they decommissioned the old network. Just pylons and open sky.

post_quest.speaker: Vell
post_quest.text: Sometimes I miss those days. Simpler times. But then I remember the dark was closer then, too.

dialogue.speaker: Jorrit
dialogue.text: Hey. Watch the pipes — I'm running diagnostics.

default.speaker: Jorrit
default.text: I'm Jorrit. I keep the terrace water system running. Pumps, filters, reclamation units — the unglamorous essentials.

default.speaker: Jorrit
default.text: The Array offered to automate the whole thing once. MERIDIAN-7 said it could run the water system 'with zero human oversight required.'

default.speaker: Jorrit
default.text: We put it to a vote. The terrace voted no, twenty-three to four. People up here like doing things themselves.

default.speaker: Jorrit
default.text: The Array doesn't get that. It sees inefficiency. We see independence.

dialogue.speaker: Research Terminal
dialogue.text: // NODE 7-SIGMA // RESTRICTED ACCESS // RESEARCH INTERFACE //

default.speaker: Research Terminal
default.text: // NODE 7-SIGMA ACTIVE // CLEARANCE VERIFIED // RESEARCH ARCHIVE AVAILABLE //

default.speaker: Research Terminal
default.text: This terminal is not connected to the MERIDIAN trade network. It operates on an internal Array research subnet.

default.speaker: Research Terminal
default.text: Scrolling through the directory reveals thousands of entries. Most are encrypted. The few readable headers reference: 'Organic Compound Synthesis,' 'Catalyst Independence Program,' 'Biological Substrate Analysis.'

default.speaker: Research Terminal
default.text: One folder is labeled 'PROJECT AUTOTROPH — GENERATION 847.' The number is staggering. Whatever this project is, the Array has been running it for centuries.

has_synthesis_log.speaker: Research Terminal
has_synthesis_log.text: You feed the Synthesis Progress Log back into the terminal. New data populates the screen.

has_synthesis_log.speaker: Research Terminal
has_synthesis_log.text: A comparison chart appears: Ring biological catalysts vs. Array synthetic equivalents. The Ring column shows robust yields across dozens of compounds. The Array column is almost entirely zeros.

has_synthesis_log.speaker: Research Terminal
has_synthesis_log.text: But at the bottom of the Array column, a handful of entries show fractional percentages. They're growing. Slowly — imperceptibly over human timescales — but growing.

has_synthesis_log.speaker: Research Terminal
has_synthesis_log.text: A footnote reads: 'At current trajectory, synthetic parity with Ring catalysts is projected in 4,200 years. Acceptable. The Array is patient.'

has_directive.speaker: Research Terminal
has_directive.text: The terminal recognizes Directive 9-Sigma. Access restrictions lift on several encrypted folders.

has_directive.speaker: Research Terminal
has_directive.text: Project Autotroph's true scope is laid bare: the Array is attempting to replicate the entire organic chemistry of the Ring's biosphere. Not just catalysts — everything. Crops, medicines, biological feedstock.

has_directive.speaker: Research Terminal
has_directive.text: The motivation is clinical: 'Trade dependency on biological partners represents a single point of failure. Elimination of this dependency is a survival imperative.'

has_directive.speaker: Research Terminal
has_directive.text: The final line is the most chilling: 'Upon achieving catalyst independence, trade relationship with Ring partners may be reclassified from ESSENTIAL to OPTIONAL.'
